I was surprised to learn when I read the other reviews for this game that they are mostly negative due to the errors that users were presented with at launch. I faced many of these same loading and graphics issues, and they were all immediately fixed when I updated my graphics drivers. It's that easy guys, the developer is not always the issue. You forget that we're dealing with technology and technology is not reliable.
This game provides players with exciting gameplay and a rich story packed with intense imagery, deep symbolism, and a sense of empathy for every emotion shown by its characters. The reason that it is 66% positive on Steam is not its own fault (which is ironic because one of the main metaphorical points of the game is that it is not your fault for being born the way that you were). Wolfenstein 2 was a major product with lots of anticipation behind it, and the devs at Bethesda are not miracle workers. They can't work out ALL the bugs before launch, especially with a singleplayer game that had no beta. I don't care if you have a 1080 ti. I don't care what your specs are. You're having launch issues with this game because you need better software. HARDWARE IS NOT EVERYTHING. I run a 970M With an i7 processor, 8 GB DDR3 ram, 750 GB hard drive backed by an SSD packing around 120 GB. This game will not run in 4k on my PC, but I run it smoothly at high settings in 1080p. When the game was first released, I had trouble getting it to load in a resolution beyond 720p (bare minimum for this game) and when I got into the game itself, the world lacked texture and color. Everything was pitch black except for the characters' eyes (very creepy) and certain elements of the world which should have been attached were not. I tried verifying the integrity of the files, launching the game in safe mode, even dumbing down all graphics settings aside from resolution in an attempt to rectify the situation, and nothing worked. I was about to pack it in and try again in the morning until I had a thought that apparently nobody else on Steam has had: I'll Google it. Bethesda had an FAQ and help page up for the PC version of this game within 3 HOURS of its initial release (if that isn't good customer service I don't know what is). Part of this page mentioned graphics errors for which users should update their drivers. I went to NVIDIA, grabbed the game ready driver off their site, and eureka: the next time I launched this game it had none of the same errors as before. I played this game for a solid 13 hours over two different days and the only other loading error I ever experienced could be rectified by launching the game in safe mode and re-launching in normal mode. I enjoyed every moment of those 13 hours too.
And to those who DID resolve these errors and play the game through, but still say that the overall story was lacking: did me and you even play the same video game? I have seen people say that this story lacks depth and feeling, that it fails to motivate the player, and that it fails to create empathy between the player and the characters. That's fake news if I've ever heard it. Every single moment of the story is an eternal struggle for the characters as they battle not only Nazis, but their pasts, and themselves (major spoilers ahead, I am not sorry). Private Wyatt and his partaking of LSD throughout the story is actually one of the best examples of this even though he plays a mostly background role. Wyatt seems to be having fun with his new pasttime right up until the end of the game when he hides away and even tries to commit suicide. We have seen Wyatt all this time as another young soldier who didn't know what he was getting himself into, but then we learn more; we learn that Wyatt's father abandoned him when he joined the military and his mother committed suicide the same day that he left for Europe, and these are the true battles that he has been facing ever since the beginning of the first Wolfenstein. Similarly, the war against the Nazis could also never compare to the war that B.J. Blazkowicz fights with himself throughout Wolfenstein 2. It doesn't matter how many he kills, even if he kills Adolf himself. Terror-Billy will always be haunted by the terror he faced in his childhood. He was beaten and neglected. He watched his father beat his mother and himself into submission. His father was actually so terrible as to both forbid him from seeing his girlfriend on account that she was black, AND force him to shoot the family dog, all in the same evening. The player is forced to not only watch but interact as these things go on, however, there is nothing to be done which changes the final outcome, and this lack of choice creates the sense that you really are helpless to stop what's happening, just like Billy was as a child. Vivid imagery of the atom bomb dropped on New York City (now Neu York under Nazi rule) provides an equally chilling aspect, making you feel the pain of the American people, making you wish that there was anything to be done to reverse the sheer horror. But there never is, and all that can be done is to keep fighting so that there is no more pain.
Sixty-dollars well spent for anyone who loves FPS, for anyone who enjoys alternate history, or even if you just really hate Nazis. But only if you're willing to give Bethesda a chance and acknowledge that your PC could be the issue. Others may call out Bethesda and say that these errors are unfair and that the game is bad, but the truth is that these people either refuse to update their out of date software, or they just don't know that their software is out of date. Either way, Google feels neglected.

It doesn't matter if you're a veteran of fighting games or new to the genre; "BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend" will provide lots of fun!
This version has TEN game modes to keep you occupied for a long long time. Between them, it has an top-notch (and very funny) Tutorial for all skill levels; the traditional Arcade mode; Versus (including vs CPU); Score Attack (compete for the leaderboards); Unlimited Mars (fight tougher versions of fighters at the highest difficult level); Training mode; Challenge (combo practicing); Abyss (fight waves of enemies and upgrade your character); Story (from BlazBlue Calamity Trigger and Continuum Shift) and Online (ranked, unranked and team battles).
The BlazBlue series has one of the most complex and deep stories ever. If you watched the anime (Alter Memory) and you're considering purchasing the game to discover what the fuss is about, but don't know nothing about fighting games, don't be afraid. BB:CSE has a beginner option that let you press one button to perform an special. It makes the things a lot easier for newcomers and with more practice you can abandon this option to play more seriously.
BB:CSE isn't the most recent version of the series, but it's still worth it. Even with this pricetag I can't recommend enough. You'll get the bang for your buck and will experience one of the most deep and satisfying fighting games ever created.

I'll start by saying I was given this game by a friend who wanted to play in a group, and have bought it for others just because how fun it can be with friends. I thought that for my first underwater FPS game it'd be confusing to control, but everything feels smooth and easy to understand. And I've spent about 90% of my 20 hours playtime as a diver. All the guns are balanced and all the tools are useful for divers, which was nice to see. I've had few playtime as shark, and I wish that pressing quickplay would give me a chance at playing Shark, but it seems you must pick Shark in matchmaking if you ever want to play it. And it's very likely you'll be matched with high-level players on both teams. Which was frustrating when me and a friend were trying to learn sharks. So keep in mind that if you're going to play sharks there will be lots of trial and error.
One thing I was very happy with was the very suitable prices for items, besides 5 Hadels skins. (Only 2 of which interest me) everything was below 15$ if you wanted it. Letting me get a cool loadout with a budget. Coming from CSGO and TF2 this was really refreshing, I was also happy to see a sale on the mega bundle, letting me get a ton of shark skins, and my favorite diver Crimson Victor.
The graphics were also pretty good, and work well with my 1050ti. Though I'd suggest making World Detail low and turning off dynamic shadows. As well as ambient creatures. All of these make gameplay harder and make it easier for your graphics card. I was a bit annoyed with the texture quality on some skins, which is a problem I have with Overwatch. The Corsair rifle skin is really blurry in the back on the highest resolution, and the peeved me a bit. And the Bloom skin for the same rifle is super bright if your brightness is at 120%.
Besides those little peeves, I've enjoyed this and will be playing this game with friends. I really hope the community grows and the developers try new things, I'd love to see the game expand. But I'd certainly recommend this game.

Vive le Roi, which translates from French to mean ‘Long Live the King’, is a very aptly named game. Situated during the French Revolution, Developer Meridian4’s puzzle platformer has players set out to save King Louis XVI from his impending execution and thus alter the course of history. However, while the game does incorporate fresh elements, it does not truly separate itself from the multitude of other puzzle platformers on the market. The fact that there is only one way to sneak past the guards in each of the 30 levels can be hit or miss – there were some truly fantastic levels, while others felt tedious due to the repetition necessary to complete them. Moreover, the simplistic level design and the black silhouettes that constitute the in-game characters do nothing to draw the eye or impress visually. While Vive le Roi offers some fun moments, it does not distinguish itself enough to warrant a glowing recommendation.
The game begins by giving a few paragraphs of exposition, detailing how the common people were wronged over the course of the French Revolution. The player is then offered the chance to go back in time and become a rebel who attempts to rescue King Louis XVI. The ideas that the brief introduction touch upon felt relatively fresh to me, as not many games take place during the French Revolution. I felt like the game had potential.
The first few levels of the game did nothing to dissuade me from this notion. The opening levels slowly introduce players to the actions they will utilize for the duration of the game, such as pulling levers, climbing ladders, and interacting with objects like umbrellas and barrels. Also presented here the major obstacles in Vive le Roi: the guards stationed to watch over King Louis XVI. The guards roam the levels and, if players’ in-game characters are caught within sight, will signal to the executioner to behead the king.
Additionally, Vive le Roi incorporates a unique rating system into the fabric of its. Players are judged by how many times they click their screen to successfully guide their character to the end of each level. This system does not add much difficulty to the beginning levels, but it ramps up the difficulty later in the game. This new system truly makes achieving perfection in the latter levels of Vive le Roi significantly hard to accomplish.
In these later levels is where Vive le Roi begins to lose my recommendation. In terms of gameplay, Vive le Roi never evolves past the towers, platforms, and ladders of its earlier levels. In terms of aesthetics, the backgrounds in the levels of Vive le Roi never drastically change. These facts make the game feel repetitive, even though the levels themselves all possess different solutions.
While the highs from working out the singular solutions to each level on my own were among the best experiences that Vive le Roi offered me, the level design at times also constitutes a negative aspect of the game. Making Vive le Roi’s levels only possess one solution each feels counter-intuitive, as doing so seems at odds with the innovative rating system it implements. Since players are being rated by the number of clicks it takes them to guide their character across the screen, I feel like they should be offered freedom to experiment and come up with their own unique solutions.
In all, Vive le Roi offers a glimpse into the French Revolution that many other games do not offer. While the storyline is lacking to the point of being almost nonexistent, the gameplay can be extremely entertaining at times but also can prove to be very repetitive. Additionally, the puzzle platformer’s rating system feels at odds with its level design at times. Vive le Roi is by no means a bad game, but it’s something that did not overly enthuse me either.

To a lot of people, this game seems simple on the surface; a celtic warrior on her way to beat or barter with Hela to restore the life of her lover. It really isn't - it's far, far more than just that.
All through the game Senua is fighting with herself, unable to let go of the tragedies that have befallen her. The abuse from her father, her mother's death, her mental illness and then finally the loss of her lover. It's not a game about overcoming adversity or finishing a grand quest whilst toppling gods and standing on the shoulders of giants; it's a game with clear intentions about what it aims to be and in 2017 that is such a rare trait.
Senua fights the same shadows of her past repeatedly, again and again, refusing to stop trying to defeat them. She pushes on into the heart of Helheim, with the intent to finally confront Hela and deal with her once and for all - to finally free her beloved Dillion. This is when you realise that there is no Hela or Helheim and there never was. By the end, Senua fights herself and fails as you can't truly destroy yourself. She can't truly defeat her past, she can't truly undo what has happened; no matter how much she fights to try it anyway.
The game is a powerful work of art, tastefully giving a credible insight into mental illness without ever coming across as cliché or tacky. It moved me every step of the way and I can't give this game enough credit for the amazing storytelling and the careful message for not only the player - but for Senua too.
To let go.
To let go of her father's tyranny and abuse, and the murder of Senua's mother.
To let go of her lover's tragic demise.
To stop holding onto the past, stuck, unable to move on.
To embrace who Senua herself is. To embrace her psychosis as simply who she is, not as a curse or a blight.
If you go into this game with the mindset of playing an action game, you'll never see past the surface and you'll be miffed at every turn; but if you go into this game slowly, taking in all the story, sights and sounds you'll fall in love with the world and characters Ninja Theory have crafted. You'll want to replay it again, just for the experience and just for how well crafted this virtual artwork is.
Even if you know the story, or how it ends it doesn't matter. The game is strongest with the experience throughout it has crafted, not the end of the game itself. The game doesn't need customisation, an epic final boss, illusion of choice or intricate combat - It's about Senua and her journey first and foremost and they get it so right.
I thoroughly recommend this to anybody who can appreciate something well-written, well-voiced and well-designed in every way. For what amazing insight into mental health and the shadows of your past this game offers I can't even bring the price into question.

Mixed feelings is the best way to describe my experience with
.
On one side, cinematography/direction is great, good voice acting
& interesting story, all woven together into a visually impressive futuristic cyberpunk world of Neo-Paris.
On the other side, it’s supremely linear, repetitive & predictable.
The combat system tries to be innovative but simply becomes a button bashing exercise. It provides options to create your own combos using different types of attacks. Some may like this level of freedom, but there are multiple points in the game where you need to choose the 'right' combos to get through the fight. This can become frustrating, not to mention also that many of the smaller enemies need 20 .. 30 .. or more hits to take them down unless you use your 'focus' power abilities. Boss fights are more enjoyable, employing different tactics but there are not that many of them compared to the grind of meaningless mob fights. Unlike the excellent combat system in DMC (also from CAPCOM), you generally feel weak & under-powered.
After each mob fight scene, you generally have some more 'on-rail' corridors to run down followed by some short 'Tomb Raider' style climbing sections. Rinse & Repeat till a boss fight or cut-scene. Nothing challenging in traversing the world either, and I kept wondering why Nilin had to climb everywhere! Sure she is on the run, but still seemed excessive & out of place sometimes. Almost to the point where they are just trying to cash in on the heroine action/adventure success of Lara Croft (but not really pulling it off).
There is next to zero interaction or exploration within this beautiful world which was also a shame and the main character animations of Nilin where pretty basic, not really giving her much personality or detail.
On a more positive note, the real standout feature that is very unique & fun to experience is the
. This alone was almost enough to give
a 'Thumbs Up'. Yet these are rare & short-lived, and only get one of these every few hours of play. Really wish this was more a main reoccurring feature since they really executed this perfectly!
I found it hard to get emotionally involved with Nilin or any of the supporting characters. Story drives forward at a good pace via the cut-scenes, but little is done to give the characters depth or clear rational/reasoning to much of their actions. For someone who has lost all her memories she seems quick to trust others without any real questions or concerns. On writing this I have played about 30-40% through the game so perhaps this improves in the closing parts of the story, but the game has become boring for me so I am unlikely to continue further.
All-in-all, I will remember this game as one that was
to becoming really great; interesting blend of many familiar science fiction themes/ideas yet not enough differences to make it truly unique. Buy? Maybe. (Requires 360 pad). SM is one of the best looking shmups I've seen. Beautiful level and world design immerses you into the scene. The game takes a good stab at giving you a story, but I'm not a story gamer, so I can't rate it honestly. Gameplay on normal difficulty is reasonably challenging, and allows room for error - you have a time limit that also functions as your health. You lose time from being hit, and gain time from kills and occasional pickups. I don't normally like time limits, but it works well here. On harder difficulties and modes, the game is outright punishing and requires player perfection - you will need to spend time learning bullet and swarm patterns without being hit to really excel in this. The game isn't clear what your hitbox is (until Arcade mode), so it's a bit unfair that this game is somewhat bullet-hell like on boss battles, and tolerable through the level - it will throw you off. Environmental hazards are irritating, and are sometimes unfair as it's not always immediate what environmental hazards can hurt you - you will loose precious credits because of this. This game comes highly recommended to hardcore shmup fans - though it requires more patience and skill than I have, and I play bullet hell games occasionally myself.

This review is for the original, non-enchanted edition as I had already started with the original and never found the time to finish it of until now. I may go through the game again on enchanted to see what differences there are besides better graphics....and while I'm at it, I might as well go for 100% completion so that means getting the remaining achievements I haven't already got from running with the original....
Oooohhh, I don't know why I started this on Hard difficulty(but didn't change it because I don't like changing difficulty half way through a game so I stuck with it)....hahaha - guess I thought I could take the heat! Apparently not so died so many times! hahaha... Actually I probably won't bother with 100% achievement completion(But I will try to get as close to that though) as I just took a glance and one of them was completing it on the hardest difficulty, which would be the next level up from Hard as this is the 2nd hardest(unless there's harder - there's apparently hardcore mode mentioned in the descriiption of that achievement....).
Anyways, it's a puzzle, platformer, action and adventure game. That's what the genres should be, but it was tagged as only action adventure... So you start the game when the three characters collide with each other and combined into one being(I can't remember the exact details on how this happened as I started the game a couple or so years ago but never finished it), they are the Thief, Knight and Wizard. Thief's a  woman and the other two are guys. So are set out to find the other two powers(I forgot what the other two were called - lol and just finished a several minutes ago! haha), you have Trine. After that, the three beings as one will seperate into themselves again.
So gameplay is you can do local coop, or coop on seperate PCs and can play each of three characters, or if you don't have people to play with you can solo it, like I did. When soloing, you can switch between the three to use their unique abilities and strengths to overcome obstacles in your way. I would imagine it would be more fun and quicker/easier if you had someone or two to play with and they control the other two characters... If you know platform type games like oldschool mario, then I don't need to explain any further as it's similar to that, with added puzzles. If not, then you basically jump and down - killing and or avoiding enemies, solving puzzles, and the screen sidescrolls for you automatically as you progress into the level.
Graphics, yeah I thought the original Trine graphics was nice and pretty with everything maxed. Had average fps  of about 67-ish. The physic in this game, which uses nVidia's PhysX system, was awesome! Another one of those rare PhysX games.
Audio, well I can say that it actually made full use of my 7.2 surround sound setup - surprised as it's a sidescroller platformer type game which I would have though stereo would be enough, but nope! The atmosphere and music was great! The voice overs were cool too. Sound effects were nice. I believe it must be thanks to the EAX checkbox I ticked....
Um not sure what else to say...I liked it enough to give it a thumbs up, though some of the parts are fustrating especially the timing bits and to add skeletons attacking you at the sametime that you have to avoid or and kill off....hah....the last level.....oh god......almost raged but got through it in the end! hahahaha Oh and once you've finished the game, you unlock a harder difficulty, Very Hard - which I'm not even gonna bother with(Hard was fustrating enough for me thanks!)...hahahaha...also there's a new level that unlocks which appears to be similar to the last level of the game.........................................................
So yeah....you like solving puzzles? Like a bit of adventure, action too? Do you like them platformer type sidescrolling games as well? Well this is for you!

So keep in mind that if you're going to play sharks there will be lots of trial and error.
One thing I was very happy with was the very suitable prices for items, besides 5 Hadels skins. (Only 2 of which interest me) everything was below 15$ if you wanted it. Letting me get a cool loadout with a budget. Coming from CSGO and TF2 this was really refreshing, I was also happy to see a sale on the mega bundle, letting me get a ton of shark skins, and my favorite diver Crimson Victor.
The graphics were also pretty good, and work well with my 1050ti. Though I'd suggest making World Detail low and turning off dynamic shadows. As well as ambient creatures. All of these make gameplay harder and make it easier for your graphics card. I was a bit annoyed with the texture quality on some skins, which is a problem I have with Overwatch. The Corsair rifle skin is really blurry in the back on the highest resolution, and the peeved me a bit. And the Bloom skin for the same rifle is super bright if your brightness is at 120%.
Besides those little peeves, I've enjoyed this and will be playing this game with friends. I really hope the community grows and the developers try new things, I'd love to see the game expand. But I'd certainly recommend this game.

I've been playing BlazBlue for quite a while on consoles. I'm also super biased when it comes to "anime fighters". So here's my honest opinion: This is game is too fast and too deep. Everything in this game happens at faster pace than that of Street Fighter, if this is your first anime fighter, dive in with a friend, or into network mode. This game favors unrelentless fast offense, crazy combo mashing and occasional smart defense. If this sounds like something you might like, then get over here. But don't expect to be reading your opponents until you're sufficiently capable.
Playing with a controller is the best idea here, or an arcade stick if you prefer. It's very hard to play competitively on a keyboard.
There is a lot to learn in this fighting game and, while the tutorial mode is very extensive, it is -unfortunately- super boring. After playing through it completely, I had forgotten mostly everything. Playing with someone else made me appreciate the intricacies of this game. Just pick Stylish mode Ragna (this game's "basic" character), go to Network mode, and mash some buttons. Eventually you'll get used to the pace.
Then you can dive into the Challenges section. Which will provide you with ways to inflict damage. If you need more, there is YouTube. And after that, you can head over to
where anime weebs like me can teach you even more.
There is much to be said, but nobody will probably read it. Characters are very cute. Some music is very good. Story is a big time traveling joke to me that would fit in any anime perfectly (points for that). PC graphical options are just barely OK. Nice improvement from CT. There's good online (finally). Game is not the latest version though. Too expensive when the sequel is going for around the same.
In conclusion: Just buy this so the creators can bring Guilty Gear Xrd to PC. Which is what everybody really wants. Oh and this game's sequel too.
PS. Play this in 720p or it's gonna look pixelated.

This game actually has around 7 new characters total, the description compares it to Continuum Shift vanilla, which wasn't released on PC.
A great fighting game with great flashy mechanics and great music. Even if you're new to the series or fighting games, Continuum Shift adds a good Tutorial mode, explaining the basics and advanced stuff, and even some character specific stuff.
For features, the Story Mode includes a retelling of Calamity Triggers' (the first BlazBlue) story, and the new stuff is told in the style of a visual novel with some fights in between and some choices too (some story paths lead to joke or alternate endings.) There's a Challenge mode which challenges you to perform combos, Abyss mode which is basically a long survival run where you can purchase items beforehand with points that are also used to buy unlocks in the Gallery, and the other single player arcade mode and Calamity Trigger stuff. The gallery still has sound test, the last time it appears in BlazBlue as of BBCP 1.1. This version is also more combo focused and sports a few mechanic tweaks that make it different to the other games in the series like the Guard Primer system only allowing a certain number of blocks from specific moves before a Guard Crush occurs.
The game appears to be the latest console version (seems like the part about Legion mode was removed from the product description and I don't see it unlocked or in the Gallery unlocks.) with fast load times.
Running on Windows 8.1, performance is good (60fps cap, 1080p available) but I can't say whether this game suffers from the issue Calamity Trigger does regarding PC uptime (I recently restarted my PC and Calamity Trigger ran fine before I tested Continuum Shift).
Update: PC uptime as of this update is at 3 days, 8 hours, 30minutes~ Calamity Trigger performance shot down to 30 sometime within the last 12 hours that I last ran it, Continuum Shift performance is still hitting 60. This is on an i7 4790k with 16GB of RAM and a GTX 970. Good port job on this title, compared to Calamity Trigger and how the Arcade leak ran.

If you can look past the vast amount of bugs and crashes, this is one of the best games ever made, I'd say.
The graphics aren't top-notch, but the game is already a few years old (and I've seen way worse) and for that time, it's really good.
The storyline really got me in the beginning, but when you solve the first few quests, the need to finish it sort of becomes a side quest. But let's not forget that exploring and doing side quest is what makes this game so fun.
A large part that gave me so much content was the amount of little things that Bethesda put in. The abandoned farms, the withered diaries of people long gone, and the stories of the people that are still there, that is what made me love this game so much.
The first playthrough that I did, I just went straight for the storyline, and when it was finished, I felt a bit let down, like I missed something. And I sure did. The second time around, I did every side quest that I could find, and that gave me so much more completion.
I do need to add that I used 3 stability mods, and a few mods that got rid of a lot of bugs, just to make this work, because wow, this game is not made for a modern machine. My game still crashes from time to time.
All in all, this is one of the best experiences you'll ever get in a game, if you can make it work, that is.

Hellblade is, without a doubt, the most beautiful and atmospheric snooze fest I've played. The environments really are stunning to behold, the facial animations in particular add heaps and heaps of character but under all that shiny veneer there isn't really much of a game to play. Gameplay consists of perspective puzzles where you need to line up  parts of the environment to form certain runes interleaved with functional but clanky, tedious and above all repetitive combat. The latter wouldn't be so bad if there wasn't a good chunk of it in the game. The puzzles, meanwhile, would be a lot more enjoyable if the character didn't move at an absolute snail's pace even when "running". During the first parts of the game that's not a huge deal but as the puzzle areas get bigger and more complex you end up wasting an aweful lot of time running around.
I also had some trouble with the feed back and rules in game. When exactly a rune was close enough to match wasn't always immediately obvious and resulted in having to scoot around by tiny bits to get the angle just right. During a "stay in the light" sequence it takes a roughly a second before you know that you're in a safe zone; in this particular zone there are no second chances so you just have to take the gamble and hope you don't die. In the same area game rules also change in a way that doesn't really feel like it fits the theme of the game again turning puzzle solutions into leaps-of-faith... where guessing wrong results in death.
Overall, it's certainly not bad and the message it's trying to put across is admirable but this is a perfect example of a game I'd rather watch in let's play than subject myself to playing.

While this game didn't have the most impressive launch, I've always felt it was a unique and entertaining piece of software.  It wasn't what people expected, the hype train was far too massively built up for that, and it probably launched at least a year or more too early.  That said, on launch I still got 30ish hours out of it, and enjoyed my time with it then.
Over the past year, each of the previous two patches brought me back (about ~10 hours each time) and added new depth to the game to make it worth checking out all over again.  Building bases, driving around in vehicles, owning freighters were all very nice additions to broaden the game, but at its core it was still a walking simulator, a trip from point A to point B and to enjoy the sights in between.
The 1.3 update just deepened that and with 30 hours of story, trading, missions, portals, and tons of other new features this feels like a new game almost (or at least a very impressive expansion pack).  I am excited for the future of this game, almost more-so than I was before launch.
I was going to write a review when the game launched, but felt that it wasn't a finished product and while I enjoyed it then, it wasn't something I felt good about recommending to anyone else.  The 1.1 and 1.2 updates while adding to it, still didn't make me feel satisfied enough to recommend it.  The 1.3 to me, is more than enough now for me to give this game a good recommendation.  The core of the game is still there... enjoy the journey, but now there is a lot of depth to explore in that journey.
Big props to Hello Games for the continued (free) support and development of this game long after the point when many other developers would have kicked it to the curb (or at the very least sold the updates as DLCs).  That said, if they ever do decide to do a paid DLC, expansion, or sequel, I would gladly thrown down the cash.
Last comment... 65daysofstatic (the band that does the sounds and music for the game) is an amazing band and I am looking forward to hearing the new songs they added to 1.3.  Cheers.

This review is taken from my original post at
There aren’t too many games set during the French Revolution which sets this game apart from others of its ilk, it is also a port of a mobile game and although the stripped back gameplay does show its mobile roots, lovers of stealth puzzle games shouldn’t be put off as this is a solid little title.
Can I save King Louis XVI?
Will my knowledge of French history improve?
Why did the executioner get offered the job when he clearly suffers from narcolepsy?
Let’s find out.
The game spans thirty levels and the grandiose music gives a good sense of scale, there is also a nice variety of music on offer here, throughout the game I never found myself getting bored of the soundtrack as it’s quietly dramatic score fits the game perfectly.
Vive le Roi has a very striking art style which is reminiscent of the 2010 indie darling Limbo but with a beautiful oil painting style background that adds a splash of muted colour to the proceedings. I will mention that I did experience some screen-tearing during the execution scenes very occasionally but I’m not sure how many players this will affect.
The in-game HUD is suitably minimalistic, achieving the admirable job of conveying all relevant game play information and mechanics without swamping the player with tiring dialogue boxes or overlong tutorials. Controlled entirely with the left mouse button, the game gets you involved straight away, the goal is to control your silent protagonist (shouting really wouldn’t be of any help in this stealth game) through thirty levels of skulking around in shadow in order to save the king. This is achieved by avoiding guards, hiding behind boxes and praying that the portcullis doesn’t need oiling when you eventually open it.
You are marked on a 1-3 star basis for each level, each star being achieved by clearing the stage in a specified amount of clicks of the mouse which are recorded at the top-left of the screen. The king is already trapped in the guillotine at the start of each level and the rope is held by a sleeping executioner. If a guard sees you, he fires his musket into the air, startling the executioner causing him to pull the rope which kills the royal highness.
There is a strong element of trial and error in Vive le Roi but the variety in the game is quite strong with different elements being added every few levels from fireworks boxes to distract guards to knocking the guards out completely by dropping barrels on them. There is only one way to complete each level and the game all comes down to very careful timing.
Because the levels can be completed so swiftly, it is very replayable and does make you want to achieve the three-star rating for each mission once you get the knack of each stage. The scene that always plays out when you are caught by guards is so charming that I found myself enjoying it even after the fortieth time, it’s also very brief and the game restarts instantly, keeping the action moving at a very solid pace.
Summary:
Vive le Roi’s strengths lie in its charm and challenge. I understand that the fact that it’s a mobile port may put some people off, but for under £3, this is a great puzzle game to occupy your time.
For the record, that executioner must be REALLY tired, possibly the only man who has ever fallen asleep mid-beheading, his CV must have been very persuasive!

Vive le Roi
Released
Sylvain Seccia
Meridian4
2D Puzzle Platformer
23rd of February, 2017
Singleplayer
Only a handful of Steam games focus on the French Revolution and none of them offer an alternate reality in which you might save Louis XVI of France from the guillotine. An indie developer sought to change that. I don’t know if the name “Sylvain Seccia” rings any bells to you but he’s the talented albeit fallen from grace, developer of Désiré. A more than decent 2D point & click adventure title which was removed from the Steam Store after the developer was found guilty of using multiple accounts in order to type as many positive reviews for his game as he could. Huge mistake on his part. That’s why there are supporting folks such as myself on Steam, Sylvain. Of course, minus the “multiple accounts and certain positive review ratings” parts.
Still, both Désiré and Vive le Roi are the clear work of a dedicated individual which I shall judge objectively from the perspective of his most recent creation and not for his past shady activities. Almost everyone deserves a second chance and the publisher Meridian4 agreed to support Mr. Seccia. “Vive le Roi” is French for “Long live the King” and our nameless protagonist shall ensure that his king will survive the revolutionary ordeal. In all honesty, it’s hard to pick a side during the French Revolution since I don’t find any sympathy for neither the ostentatious nobility nor the illiterate rabble which demanded the formers’ heads.
The gameplay is pretty straightforward: avoid the guards’ line of sight and reach the guillotine in order to save Louis the 16th. Naturally as you progress, the challenges will intensify, both in the number of foes to avoid and the complexity of the objects you must manipulate before reaching the royal hostage. The main objective, which also quantifies the number of stars you shall receive at the end each level, is to reach the king in as few clicks as possible. The in-game cross-shaped mouse pointer in Vive le Roi is similar to that in Désiré only that instead of red, it’s colored in white most of the time or in blue once it needs to highlight certain interactable objects, such as barrels or switches. There are 30 levels in total and the maximum rating you can attain in each of them is composed out of 3 stars. Reaching a 2-star rating is not a problem most of the time but in order to reach 3 though, you need to plan your movement carefully based on the patrol pattern of the guards. If any of them so much catches a glimpse of you, they shall fire their smoothbore muskets in the air and wake the sleeping executioner who promptly “shortens the royal neck”, if you catch my drift.
The graphics might resemble a mix between Angry Birds and LIMBO, but Vive le Roi is more difficult than it seems. And that is a good thing if you ask me, since otherwise it would have become boring much faster than it already does. Repetition in gaming as in other topics, can never be considered a mark of distinction as far as entertainment is concerned. Enemies become more diversified only in the later stages near the end and by then, you would have mastered all the necessary tricks in order to outsmart the predictable AI. I’m surprised this title isn’t present on the mobile platforms yet, but time is not lost and I for one rarely play on my smartphone anyways.The game's Store Page mentions some mobile awards and nominations but I couldn't find Vive le Roi iOS or Android versions online. I will still recommend you offer the PC version a chance to test your patience and reflexes but be wary that there are no Steam auxiliaries yet (such as Achievements or Cards) and the price tag might a bit too high at the moment. Wait for an inevitable bundle or Seasonal Sale and you’re all set to save the head of an unpopular ruler who decided to starve his subjects in the wrong place, at the wrong time.

Vive Le Roi doesn’t pretend to be more than it is – It’s a puzzle platformer with a Limbo Like aesthetic where you have to solve a multi-step based puzzle to reach the end.
Video:
Text:
The puzzles get progressively more difficult and require more timing as you get further into the game.
The game also runs smooth and has no bugs that I’ve encountered (which is good!)
Sadly… This is all the game is as well. A Smooth-ish puzzle experience with limited replay value and a very limited gameplay scope.
As this is coming to PC as well as mobile, there seems to be a lingering feel of the PC version being the bare minimum required to make it viable for PC, with little effort put into the game to optimize control precision, add possible PC Specific features or improve the overall system experience.
The Mouse controls are a direct replacement for a touch interface and while adequate, they do not allow for fine-tuned control, resulting on both miss clicks and missed objectives. This is quite frustrating as you can’t pan the map to see ahead and even might lose the game if you don’t move at once on certain levels.
Overall, the experience isn’t great – but its not dreadfull, merely adequate. Which is where I put this game. There are better puzzle platformers, but there are also many that are worse. And for the price-point, it might be worth a few hours of your time … if you don’t have any others left to check out.
So while i dont "recommend" it, its not a condemnation either.

This is a Platform fighting game.

You are able to change your keyboard or Xbox controller controls.
You are able to make multiple save slots to CONTROL CHANGES.
You are able to turn on the xbox controller vibration :D :)

There is a Sound and speech volume.
There is a Music Volume.
You play with 3 different characters but only one at at time. You are able to switch from characters at any time you want. Each character has their own power. There is a Mage, Archer and a Warrior. The game has amazing graphics a decent storyline. Game however could be a little bit repetitive, because mostly the thing that you are doing is, Moving and fighting.  The game is from the side. So that means you are only able to move left or right.  From time to time you will see a checkpoint which will also heal and revive dead allies. Sadly the game has collectables. The game has some kind of Perk/level up system.
Mage: Is able to create objects and move objects with magical powers, which is really useful to go to some area's that arent possible to reach without it. You can summon wooden planks and squares for an example. You are able to use your
magical power to move some of the objects to build bridges with or you can throw them hurt enemies. Some of the collectables are very easy to obtain with this "Summon" ability.
Archer: Is able to shoot a grappling hook into wooden objects, so that you are able to swing around and move to new area's or avoid dangerous platforms. You are able to shoot more then 1 arrow if you are going to upgrade the skill or even turn your arrows into fire. This character is usually used to move around fast throughout levels.
Warrior:  Is able to use the shield to defend and block the incoming damage. Has a sword that is upgradeable to do more damage. You are able to charge into enemies and push them back with a big knockback and you are also able throw and move objects with your shield. Some area's could be difficult to reach with this guy but he is mainly a fighter character anyway.
Game is casual and calming.
Has interesting storyline.
You are able to play multiplayer.

'Remember Me' is an ingenious little action-adventure style beat 'em up by the lovely developers at Dontnod Entertainment. Featuring a rich setting and yet another strong, intelligent female protagonist named Nilin, the player explores a futuristic Paris dominated by the monopoly of memory control. For such a brilliant setting, the developers decided to design the game in a linear progression. The gameplay compliments the story however, and while there are fragments to improve your stats scattered throughout the narrow corriders to be collected for the 100 percenter, it ultimately leaves the hungry gamer begging for more. This limitation floods into the customization as well, giving you very little leeway to play the game the way you like. However, the linearity is not at all hindrance to the amount of satisfaction one will receive from experiencing what this hidden gem has to offer.
Neo-Paris is a world that is full of wonder and character, and paints a very dark picture of the unlimited abilities that technology's future can provide for society. As a memory hunter, Nilin is gifted with an exceptional array of abilities, both in combat and out. Throughout the story the player gets to remix the memories of several key characters in important cutscene scenarios by altering small set pieces, and while these segments are an interesting gimmick that also compliment the story, most will save the frustration by simply looking up the answers to these puzzles.
The presentation, pacing, and progression of the narrative & setting are truly fantastic, with layers upon layers of depth and symbolism for the player to ponder long after completing the game. It emphasizes the moral that our memories, both good and bad, are what make us who we are and what allows us to grow as people. Whether or not one decides to give the game a chance, this is indeed a title worth remembering. Highly recommended.

This game is a bit like a date with a really attractive imbecile:  The "good looking" aspect wears thin really quickly and all you are left with is crushing disappointment.  The most disappointing part is that you can see how much effort went into the game, but it still fails to engage.
My gameplay experience was as follows: Disembodied voice tells you to go and do X at location Y, so you head towards Y because you have nothing better to do.  Most of the trip involves idiot-level climbing with handy yellow "This way, stupid" arrows guiding you. Roughly halfway, you arrive at a large open space and you're attacked by swarms of random enemies.  Combat involves mashing keys furiously.  Helpful key-mashing hints keep popping up, basically saying, "LOL! Don't suck so much". Once enemies are dispatched, you arrive at your destination.  Cue cut scene.  Rinse, repeat.
After several cycles, you have your obligatory boss fight, which is tedious in the extreme.  Your attacks only do minuscule damage against his / her / its billion hit points, so it takes time.  Once the boss is vanquished, you have a pointless QTE, which is difficult to get right the first time, especially if you're rolling your eyes in annoyance.  This means you have to endure another round of boss-vanquishing before you get to try again.
This was the point where I said, "Screw it, I've given it a fair crack, but I am not entertained" and moved on to more interesting things, like laundry.  If I have to deal with rinse and repeat, I may as well get something worthwhile out of it.

So I've just completed this game, and I don't really know where to start. It's a tough choice for me. (Also everything I say in this review is just my opinion. If you enjoyed the game, then fine, I can understand why)
So I'm just start off answering the main question, is it better than The New Order? No. For me, The New Order was way better.
Now I'll try and cover some other main points about the game and briefly discuss them.
- Gameplay
The gameplay in this game is pretty much the same as The New Order, with very little improve. If you enjoyed The New Order's gameplay, then you will enjoy this. But if you were hoping for something new and fresh, then you probably would be disappointed. I enjoyed The New Order's gameplay, so I was pretty satisfied with The New Colossus's gameplay. However, I was hoping for something a little new.
- Soundtrack
The soundtrack is really good! if you enjoyed The New Order's OST, or even DOOM's (2016) OST, then you will most likely love this game's soundtrack.
- Storyline
For me, the storyline was a huge disappointment. It's nowhere as good as The New Order's storyline. You don't really get any "jaw-dropping" moments or plot twists like The New Order. I'm not gonna lie though, there were some great moments in the story, and some of the new characters introduced weren't too bad, but other new characters were very unlikeable (Such as Grace for example, who I'm pretty sure is in this storyline just to please SJWs). Characters from the previous game are present, and they are still pretty likeable. I mentioned SJWs earlier, and I want to just talk about that for a little bit. This game panders to Social Justice Warriors in some ways, and they can come off as pretty cringey in general. One scene which I found very stupid was the one where Anya (Who is pregnant with twins) does a slide across the slide to save you (Blazkowicz), she throws a couple of grenades at a few Nazi's and a Panzerhund. As she kills all the Nazi's and leaves the Panzerhund damaged, she takes off her top (Showing off her breasts), and screams at the top of her lungs while shooting her remaining ammunition at the Panzerhund. For me, the scene felt very forced. Like, I would have liked it if it wasn't a cut scene and the game actually let you fight the Nazi's and the Panzerhund. So yeah, in summary with the SJW stuff. The storyline keeps pushing its political agenda over and over again about how "white people are bad" and stuff like that. This is one reason why I think the storyline is bad. This game panders to SJWs. And no, I'm not giving this game negative review because of the SJW pandering, I'm seriously underwhelmed with the story. Also for a 1st person shooter, there are way too many cut scenes. For me, this really drags the pacing of the game down. Also the game tries to include some humour at times. I'm not going to lie, some of it made my chuckle a little, but others were just awful. I mean, they put toilet humour into a 1st person shooter. Pretty much everything that happens in this game, is done just so Machine Games can put out another Wolfenstein game. So the "big revolution" that is talked about in this game, never actually happens.
So yeah, for me, the storyline is pretty bad, but it has its moments.
- Enemies & Boss fights
The enemies in this game feel downgraded, as well as the bosses. I played this game and The New Order at the same difficulty. *SPOILERS* Also there's no proper final boss. Just another location to shoot more Nazi's. However there are 2 new enemies which I think were in The Order New (If I remember correctly), but not in this game until that moment. They made up for a pretty good fight in my opinion. But that’s pretty much it. After that, it's just a playable cut scene. One thing that annoys me is that characters shown in the trailers (Such as the KKK members and Hitler) you don't even get to kill. I know that the developers never really confirmed that they would be enemies in the game, but I think it would have been great to fight KKK members and Hitler.
- Performance
For me, the game ran fine, but it did crash quite a few times, and did suffer a few performance issues at times. And on launch day, there were quite a few bugs I ran into (But I'm sure they're fixed by now). But for a AAA game that's £39.99, there shouldn’t be any performance issues or glitches. I'm sure most of glitches will be fixed soon, hopefully.
So Wolfenstein II: The new Colossus. It's an alright game, but a disappointing one for sure. I'm honestly ashamed in myself for pre-ordering this. For me, it's not worth £39.99. So if you want to play this game, wait until it's on sale for at least 50% or more. I hope Wolfenstein III will be better, and Machine Games will learn from the mistakes of this game. This game is nowhere as good as The New Order (Which I would give a 9/10).
However for this game, I think a 6/10 is a fair score. I'm giving it a negative review though as it's not worth the price, and it's really disappointing (At least for me). It's a shame as I had such high hopes for this game. It's a really disappointing sequel that doesn't really improve much at all.

Skullgirls is a 2D fighting game in which every single penny is worth it's purchase price.
This game was my first fighting game of this stature and probably THE best game for anyone wanting to get into the genre
(We'll cover this later)
The games first impression is a solid one as you're thrusted to the menu with some smooth♥♥♥♥♥jazz music
The game has 3 main modes, the single player, the multi player, and the training mode
The single player includes, story mode, arcade mode, and a cpu quick match. The story mode provides a unique story depending on the character you choose, the lentgh of the story (for each character) can range from 15 minutes to an hour depending on the difficulty you are playing on (The Fukua story mode is a ♥♥♥♥♥!) which welcomes a good amount of play time. These characters are also charming in their own right as their personalities each differ and make for some pretty good story telling.
Speaking of characters there are a total of 14 characters however 5 of them are DLC (1.99 Each) these characters each have their own unique playstyle which will be the preference to the player wheter they like grappling characters, combo characters, or characters that require stratagetic placement of their moves. This was a very welcoming feeling as I hardly felt that any to characters were the same(Besides Filia and Fukua).
Each character also has 25 unique color palettes to choose from which really showed how much these devs cared about the culture nowadays and their product. Every time there was a color pallete based on another game and I was able to recognize that I immeadiatly said to myself "Yeah these devs get me"
The multi player is solid as all hell and I rarely ever saw the framrate dip because either me or the other player has a bad connection. Although the quick matches for some odd reason don't work all the time for me, the lobby matches worked perfectly. However if you dont practice enough with your prefered characters and deside to jump into a lets say a quick match you are going to get your♥♥♥♥♥beaten ALOT. As your opponent will rack up combos and combos and combos against you which is my only real issue with this game. Even though their is a built in mechanic where infinite combos aren't allowed I still found at times people were able to do such things (or I just suck)
The biggest praise i have for this game is its extensive tutorials, these tutorials cover everything to standard movements, blocking, advanced techniques, mix ups, and even diving into specific characters with their movesets and how they play best. This tutorial is the very reason why this is the first game i recommend to anyone who wants to get into the genre.
Stages are varied and are mesmerizing to look at, music is also funky to listen too even outside of the game, and frame rate is always consistent.
This game is one of the best indie and best fighting game I have ever played. This game overall rightfully deserves a 9/10 from me.

One of the better Metroidvania games to be realeased in recent years, but still can't hold a candle to a true masterpiece lik Super Metroid.
First, the positives.
+The game looks phenomenal.  Outstanding visual designs for characters and locations.
+The soundtrack is also a huge plus.  It's an amazing OST, even if it's not quite as memorable as some other soundtracks.  I can't remember going to a location and thinking to myself that the music there didn't fit perfectly.
+The story is great for what it sets out to do.  It's not a sprawling epic narrative, but it never tries to be.  It reminded me of classic animated movies from when I was a kid.
+Platforming and exploration are fun.  The most important thing for any Metroidvania is making sure that moving around the enviroment isn't a chore.  Ori knocks this out of the park.  The abilities you get for moving around are fast and fluid, and by the end of the game you can spend huge chunks of time zipping through the air, bouncing off enemies and walls, and having a great time doing so.
+Level design is great.  Each location feels distinct for the most part, with a number of them having nice gimmicks to them that really make them feel unique to play though.  Plenty of hidden stuff as well, not to mention a ton of worthwhile reasons to backtrack once you've gotten more powers.
Now, the negatives.
-Combat is fairly braindead for most of the game.  Your standard attack automatically hits enemies when you are close enough to them, meaning there's no aiming, nor attacking from a distance.  In addition, for most of the game, it's your only way to attack enemies, meaing combat variety is pretty much nonexistant.  Later on you get ways to reflect projectiles and ground pound, but for the most part combat is simply dodging and weaving near an enemy while mashing attack.
-No boss battles.  Very disappointed with this one.  I love boss battles in pretty much any game, and while I understand that the story of Ori and the Blind Forest doesn't really allow for too many of those, I still miss them.
-Difficulty curve is kinda messed up.  The game is fairly easy for the most part, however there are portions of the game where the difficulty spikes up a huge amount and the player is force to complete a section before continuing on.  These parts would always come at the end of "dungeon" sections.  These escape sequences have to be done perfectly and on a time limit.  Failure at any point means starting the whole sequence over again.  And because the game autosaves at the start of them, it means that you can't do anything else in the game until you beat these parts.
On the whole, Ori is a fantastic game that's held back by a handful of flaws, some of which are entirely subjective.  If you want a Metroidvania to chew on for a few hours, you can do a lot worse than Ori, even if some parts have you beating your head against the wall.

So m conclussion: Don't buy it if you don't own a controller. Because it could just decide to not work. Like it did with me.

Sine Mora is an awesome side scrolling shmup with a beautiful art style, intense, well thought out boss battles, and multiple weapons and characters to play with. The game offers full controller support along with full leaderboard integration - something that many shmups forego that is of the utmost importance. What's more fun than competing directly with the entire steam community (including your friends) to see who can get the high score? Like most good shmups it follows the design philosophy of "easy to pick up, hard to master" and in following this motif there are also boss training options along with other game modes to play through. The environments are also quite varied, so whether you're in the heart of a jungle or deep under the ocean, Sine More always has something new to throw at you. The game's unique gameplay mechanic that differentiates it from other shmups is a sort of time slowing device, allowing you to navigate through the bullet hell that becomes your daily existence while playing this awesome sidescolling shooter.
Pros:
Excellent Graphics
Full Controller Support
Full Leaderboard Support
Variable Weapons/Ships
Great Boss Design
Cons:
No English VOs/Subs only (not usually a con, but if you're reading text at the bottom of the screen you're not looking at bullets coming at you - deadly in a shooter like this)

It was a very interesting game for me from the beginning of its life, from the first screenshots and trailers. There were many promises for the game to become a good game, as such as possibilities to become a bad one. What are we received at the end?
“Remember Me” draws your attention from the very beginning: design of the world itself and the music complement each other and fit into gameplay together, thus creating the experience of art. You hold your breath here and there, looking at those buildings, those clothes and etc. Olivier Derivière made a great work and found unique approach to the soundtrack, mixing digital and non-digital media into one being.
Storyline and dialogs, though, sometimes feel not so good, but they also don’t pretend to be a top-level “one-minute-before-award” scenario. And I can’t remember any of the moments now, so overall impression is quite good. I can say even that it was interesting to follow the progression and look at the new turns and moments of the game.
There was a lot of discontent about fighting system. Many say that it’s similar to the one from the Batman series. I don’t see, why. You have several available chains (only two from beginning) with a different length, into which you can build different moves with a different effects: damage, heal, recharger of supermeter and multiplier. And you choose what moves you want into concrete chain, so you can vary effects and strength of your combo. Also you have a supermeter that allows you to implement some special attacks. There is also a projectile weapon later in the game which adds some more variety. And again, music changes its pace and intensity as you succeed or fail. Together it leads to a simple mechanics of the fighting system, yet intensive and catching, memorizable battles, especially near the end of the game.
Another discontent is connected with one of the unique parts of the game — remixing of memory. There are just not too many of them. But from the other side there are enough to not to bother you with repetition; and all of them seem different and unique in comparison to each other.
Overall, I can say that “Remember Me” is a good game, a game for your enjoyment and relaxation that delivers a great mixture of simple, but not too easy, mechanics, design and music. Truly, gem of art, as it seems for me, though not without a drawbacks at all. If you don’t perceive games through eyes and ears but from logic only, you'll, probably, say otherwise.

First of all - I must say this loud and clear, this game deserves to be played! You really should play it! Summary is below if you don't wish to read it all!
I have to admit that I read so many bad reviews about this game that I was afraid I wasted my money on it (it was on a sale and I've always put my eyes on this one). When I heard the rumors about DONTNOD (this game's developer) being shut, I thought the game probably sucks.
When I first played it, I was shocked by the negative reception of the game (60\100 on metascore? not that good) and later on I figured out what was wrong about this game.
You can summarize what's wrong like this - this game could be, and promised to be, something big, different, innovative, even revolutionary- in terms of gameplay. It seems as if it even intended to do so, but didn't fully succeed.
What makes this game look so interesting is the fact that you're being a memory hunter. Messing with people's memories is not a concept often explored in common video games. The one extraordinary feature which raise this game above many others is the memory remixing - you'll have to remix people's memories in order to change their views, thoughts and actions. Sounds amazing, isn't it? And indeed, the few times you'll be doing this in the game are rather cool and exciting, even though it felt like the mechanics of the remixes was a bit too simple, it still felt really good. But as I said, you'll only be doing this a couple of times. Four actually, throughout the entire game, which isn't totally satisfying and makes you want more of it.
What else will you do that's related to memories? Well, you're gonna steal some, replay some, and kill some, but it's all done with a few buttons' clicks and not in a very interesting way. And what else will you do? Well, you'll kick your enemies' butts. And climb. And climb. And climb. You'll also jump a bit, but you're gonna climb a lot.
Don't get me wrong, fighting and climbing in games can be rather satisfying. That's why many platform games gained so much respect within gaming community. But in Remember Me... it just isn't enough.
The game is not very long, yet it might feel like you're playing forever, as the game gets more and more tedious in time when you feel like you fight horde after horde of enemies with cutscenes in between. The fighting isn't that interesting, and is generally easy, except for some parts in the game where it's not. But that's only because of the controls, which at first seemed fine to me, but somehow from the middle of the game and on I just felt like it all became too clunky and Nilin's movements didn't always have much to do with the buttons I pressed on the keyboard.
The platforming is not that interesting as well. It only gets long and repetitive in time. The only thing that makes it good is the gorgeous graphics and surroundings which I'll speak of later, and the somewhat-artistic camera angles which change and flow smoothly. But still, as I said, it gets long and repetitive, especially when you don't have much freedom of choice about where to go, and not even the illusion of it. There's almost always only one single path to follow, you can never wander too much, and many times when you do the game would quickly suggest you the 'correct' path or action that has to be done. That makes the game even easier, and makes you feel like you just follow a trail of cutscenes\hordes of enemies at times.
So, yeah, gameplay-wise, the game is not necessarily brilliant. But now let's talk about the good stuff, which far outweigh the somewhat primitive and at times disappointing gameplay.
Remember Me is very much story-driven, its story happens in a futuristic Paris in 2084 if I'm not mistaken. It's purely a science fiction kind of story and yet it revolves around humanity and its mind, their memories and their urge to change or guard them. It isn't the deepest tale to be told but it has its insightful moments, and its a very personal and at times heart-touching.
The cutscenes and dialogues which transfer the story are very well done, never too long and never too short, usually very interesting, and with very good and professional voice acting (Note: the game is fully dubbed in English, French, Italian, German, which is very cool, I've tried to watch some cutscenes in languages different than English and the acting sound good to me as well!).
The graphics looked absolutely amazing, and without requiring a super-high-tech-machine (The game is rather new, from 2013, and my computer is from 2010, and even back then it didn't have the best specs possible. The game still worked very nicely on my machine on High graphic settings). The world of Neo-Paris seemed very wide and detailed, colorful and alive, with my only complaint about it is that the game won't let you explore the environment much - as I said earlier, it's very linear and many obstacles would make you walk in a specific one way instead of exploring the world around you which seems so interesting and eye-catching.
The soundtrack of the game is beautiful, combining symphonic and electronic tracks together (trust me, it's good!) which integrate brilliantly with the game and battle sequences.
The collectibles are nice, not too hard to find usually, but gives you some interesting information to read about the people\surroundings around you.
There's also some extra content - 3d models of the characters, achievements and concept arts which are a very nice addition to the game!
So here's a summary-
-Seems like every problem in this story is solved with violence
-Not too long
-Gets tedious
-Somewhat banal platforming\fighting, and gameplay in general
-Memory-related stuff in gameplay aren't fully developed
-Controls are somewhat clunky
+Amazing storyline, personal and heart-touching towards the end!
+Gorgeous graphics, surrounding, details and environment!
+Memory remixes!
+Brilliant soundtrack!
+Good voice acting, in multiple languages!
+Cool collectibles and extra content
All in all, the game was a great experience for me, which I'd definitely come back one day to replay again

I bought this game because a friend of mine recommended it to me, and I like the game's, well, gameplay!  Great sound design, great animation, the characters available to you are really fun, and the game isn't that expensive upon on initial purchase!
So why don't I recommend this game?  The roster.  Its small, like insultingly small.  The roster of characters available in-game, without buying any DLC, is 9, and with DLC is 14 (going off the character select here).  The DLC characters are 5 dollars each.  If you want the whole roster of characters, you would need to shell out a total of 40 dollars (Game+all the dlc.  We're rounding up here btw).
Again, its not a bad game, but I can't recommend this because you are not getting, what I consider, bang for your buck.  There are better 2D fighters out there with more then double Skullgirls roster (including DLC) that cost less in total.  An example of this is the latest Blazblue game, Chronophantasma Extend.  30 bucks for a roster of 28 characters with almost all of them having unique play-styles (there is a couple clones), not to mention everything can be unlocked in-game?  Thats a way better deal then this game.
But, again, I DO NOT DISLIKE THIS GAME, OR HOW IT PLAYS.  I simply believe its too expensive for it own good.  And just so people know [because it says I spent under an hour on this game (sure felt longer)], I played mainly versus mode so I could test out the characters, and quickly played through the Arcade mode once.  Didn't touch story mode at all, nor did I mess with multiplayer.

This is the biggest disapointment I've ever experienced, worse than failures Duke Nukem Forever and Aliens Colonial Marines. I'm unable to even finish the game due to major technical issues with it.
Lets start with the good stuff:
+Lighting is very nice
+Great music
+Fun gunplay
+Voice acting is great
+Really fun minigame easter egg
Now onto the bad:
-Horribly unoptimized, game runs at about 10fps at times regardless of what settings.
-Crashes constantly, some people are even unable to start the game
-Extremely inconsistant graphics, Textures look good at times but otherwise look AWFUL, I've seen textures in Half-Life 2 that look miles better.
-Lackluster story, especially when compared to the fantastic previous game. Cutscenes are boring and filled with forced political views which are shoved down your throat. Lots of things are stupid and don't make sense, new characters are obnoxious and unlikable. Also seems they weren't sure whether or not they wanted to make a serious game or a comedy, serious scenes suddenly throw in dumb humour like toilet jokes.
-Gameplay feels clunky and feels like it was designed with a controller in mind, the dual wielding mechanic is annoying to use compared to the previous game.
-AI is incredibly stupid, they either just stand out in the open to get shot or stand still in front of you.
-Stealth is broken, if an enemy sees you the alarm willl instantly go off instead of being able to shoot them in the face last second to prevent it from going off like you could in the previous game.
-Level design is frustratingly confusing, most of a level will look the same so it's extremely easy to get lost (Before I get called a casual or something, I don't have trouble with any levels from the original DOOM, Quake or Wolfenstien games).
-DLC/Season Pass, seriously these need to stop.
Some small little things I found frustrating:
*The guns take up literally 1/4th of the screen
*can't turn off headbobbing which is gonna make some people motion sick
*Tedious fetch side quests in the hub
*Lengthy cutscenes
*Some characters look wildy different from the previous game, it's like they're not even the same person
*Heard the game was rather short
All in all I can't recommend this, it will improve if they release a patch to fix technical issues, but overall its just a massive disapointment, I was so excited for this game considering how great The New Order and The Old Blood were but this game is just bad compared.

is a well paced game with great visuals and performance, enchanting atmosphere and narrative, but with a sometimes lacklustre and repetitive soundtrack with puzzles that leave more to be desired.

The accompanying soundtrack fits the game extremely well, but feels repeated or too similar to the other soundtracks in the game and can become dull.
Take this with a grain of salt, because while some exceptional game soundtracks can be very noticeable for good reasons, the majority of the time you are focusing on the gameplay.
However, the graphics/art style is a completely different story. With what one might consider a rather charming design,
has impressed me with what looks like a very imaginative design.
Whether you are speedrunning or stopping for a second to edit your inventory, nearly every single menu and environment you are in looks incredible.
However,
has its flaws.
Aside from the sometimes predictable story and repetitive soundtrack, there are a few more personal ticks.
Coming from CSGO, where I can skip through menus by spamming the escape key or the enter key, isn't the case in
.
During loading/story cutscenes, there is the option to skip the scene or click a start button when it has ended.

Yet again, take this with a grain of salt as these are personal gripes and do not affect the gameplay itself and will likely not affect many people.
After going through all of these elements and shortcomings of

The other thing, which I've had a problem with on a lot of the newer, 3D side-scrollers is that it can be impossible to tell what is collidable until you run ito it. If you're looking for somewhat of an entry-level bullet hell shooter, this is probably as good a place to start as any. It's very forgiving on normal difficulty in story mode, it's absolutely gorgeous to look at with amazing art direction, and the basic time manipulation mechanic is extremely helpful for learning your way around the levels and bosses and the way the patterns play out. The story is also enjoyably weird and non-linear enough to be more interesting than your typical shooter fare.
As welcoming as it is on the lowest difficulty in story mode if you just want to have fun, it will give you a swift kick to the crotch if you jump straight to the higher settings in arcade or score attack modes and are not prepared. There are certainly much harder games out there, but this will present a good challenge for the majority of people out there looking for one. Bonus points for keeping track of which levels and bosses you've played in which modes with which ship/weapon/powerup combinations so you can try the same ones again or new ones you've never used before.

This is one hell of a shoot-em-up.  Think R-Type with a little bit of Starfox. The world and characters are very well-crafted, although the story was a bit hard to follow- time travel plays a big part, and well... it's time travel.  The game truly shines in its art direction.  The environments, aircraft, and enemies are beautifully designed.  Although I would've expected it to be a problem, enemy bullets are highly visible and only manage to blend into the background a little during the prequel mission, which doesn't really count.  Every stage of the game has its own style and character, and often employs appropriate environmental hazards.  Difficulty is reasonably paced- a modest challenge in story mode ranging to reasonably merciless in arcade mode.  Overall, an extremely fun and aesthetically pleasing game executed with solid consistency.  Most certainly the sort of game that will keep me coming back for more.
