I just finished the game and was so moved by the whole experience that I just had to review it - my first review for any game in fact. I'm no professional game reviewer, of course, but I hope that this can help whoever comes across this review to decide if this game is for them. I'll try to keep this as concise and short as I can.
I'll start by saying that this game is not for everybody, and that is a GOOD thing. Trying to pander to too many markets results in a very diluted product and I am happy to say that Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice is one of the few AAA games that doesnt' fall into that trap. This game is a work of art. It's an intense, narrative-driven experience that'll have you on edge every step of the way. It immerses you in a a story about a young woman's struggle with mental illness told in a way that hasn't been done before - with unrelenting honesty, detail, and love. I'd be more specific, but that would invovle spoilers, so I'll leave it at that.
The audio is phenomenal, the graphics are drop-dead gorgeous, and the motion capture/facial animations are top-of-the-line fantastic. So let's talk about the combat. The combat is just right. Meaning, too much freedom and it both takes away from the feeling of suspense and from the groundedness of Senua's capabilities. Not enough freedom and it just isn't fun.  The combat falls rightly in the middle. It's simple, but satisfying. Also, to be fair, there's actually a surprising amount of depth to the combat if you look for it. I've seen clips of other players pulling off some beautiful combos. (Made me realize how badly I was playing the game.)
Now let me tell you what this game is NOT. If you're looking for lots of customization, hack and slashing through hordes of mindless enemies, mindblowing combat mechanics, hundreds of hours of filler gameplay, or a casual and/or light-hearted experience then this game is not for you. Basically, if you're not looking for an intense narrative-driven experience then I'd probably say hold off on getting this.
But if you ARE looking for a heavily immersive and compelling narrative-driven experience, one that breaks the mold - then this game is DEFINITELY for you. And personally, I feel like calling it a narrative-driven experience doesn't do it enough justice. This game is a masterpiece and a work of art. All the elements (the gameplay, the concept, the mechanics, the performance, the atmosphere, the story) come together and synergize so perfectly. Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice is an EXPERIENCE period. If that's what you're looking for, go and get this game now.

Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice is a riveting journey about Senua, a young Celtic warrioress suffering from severe mental psychosis. She is in pursuit of her murdered husband, and finds herself in the very depths of Norse hell in order to find him.
Senua's Sacrifice explores what the media has driven to the taboo: schizophrenia and psychosis. You are placed in the shoes of one such woman who sees the world from an entirely different perspective. In a world before our time filled with ignorance and cruelty, Senua must struggle with the demons of her past, mind-numbing illusions, and unfathomable horrors in order to find the love that was taken from her.
A hack-and-slash journey of sorrow and anguish, Hellblade is a beautiful visual and story-telling masterpiece that not only takes you into the mind of a schizophrenic, but also explores the mystical mythology of the Vikings and their gods.
I haven't played a game this emotionally daunting since SOMA.

Bought this game yesterday since my Steam Library lacked controller friendly RPG's. Managed to finish it in about 12h. I'm surprised I never heard much about the game before. It's by no means a great or even good game but it hits the right spot for someone searching for a game "like God of War but"(TM) with decent voice acting (great on PAN's side) and a diverse skill point system.
In terms of graphics they look good by my standards, and they hold up very well (think Dragon Age Origins). Gameplay-wise, it's the unwanted child of Mass Effect and God-of-War, a jack of all trades - master of none cliche. 3 quaters through the game I edited the config file and set the damage multiplier to zero since there was nothing going on for me with the combat, and I wanted to push forward with the story.
As for the story, it's an interesting spin on the Jason and the Argonauts tale (love what they done with Medusa). I'd say the re-inventing of the mythological tale is this game's strong point. Overall I say buy it. I won't change your world, overheat your PC or give you something to talk about in the pub over a few beers. But it's there and it's nice, well worth the ~10 euros it demands.

Long story short: The game is good, it has some minor flaws but overall it's a nice action-adventure you're in for!
I'd rate this game somewhere in the area of a strong 7.6 and I do recommend this game.
So is this game for you?
It is if you're into the theme of ancient greek mythology, enjoy a hack n slash brawler-type gameplay and don't mind a heavy emphasis on story.
You'll recognize gameplay style and mechanics from games such as KOTOR, God of War and Mass Effect. A word of warning though, Rise of the Argonauts never really excels in either of the areas it has borrowed its style and mechanics from.
For example, the combat is nowhere near as fluid or satisfying as that you experience in God of War. The RPG elements and branching story mechanics is nowhere near as fleshed out as they are in KOTOR or Mass Effect.
Don't let that discourage you though, because even though the game doesn't reach the heights of some of its inspiration, what's there is well enough for you to see the journey through to the end. Also the games' setting, theme, story and characters are great and will keep you plenty entertained from start to finish.
Oh and I hate even bringing this subject up but I know that for some of you, it really matters a lot. I'm talking about the fact that the game isn't exactly the newest and it does show. At least if you allow yourself to compare it to modern games. Personally I think the visuals of the game are very pleasing and didn't impact my score of the game negatively in any way. With that said I do admit that it doesn't hold the standard of razor-sharp HD standards that we enjoy today. However if you let that get int the way of playing and enjoying this game then I can only say shame on you and may hades claim you!
Finally - At the current Steam price of €9 (or your local equivalent), you really can't go wrong with picking this game up.

After purchasing this game and playing it for a few hours I have come to the conclusion that it was worth buying.
The developers of this game truly have put in a lot of work towards creating an expereince which incorporates a variety of factors that must be fulfilled in order for one to be succesful, thus creating an equally interesting and challenging experience for the player.
While the graphics are certainly up to a satisfactory standard the gameplay itself gets a little stale after a while - not necessarily because there aren't enough events occuring throughout the game but rather because of its very nature.
There is only that much that the developers can do with this particular type of Indie-game, but what bothers me at times is the limited speed of the characters movement, the events occuring in response to such, and the repetitve events in response to my actions.
To sum it up:
Pros;
- Detail-rich gameworld
- Interesting characters, each with their own unique personality
- A pleasing limit of resources (e.g. money) that create scenarios in which it is crucial to make a decisive choice
- The humour of the game itself (Chickenistan)
- Blend of politics, economics, and military strategy
Cons;
- Slow movement of the characters, thus prolonging the game unnecessarily
- Repetitive personalities despite the fact that the characters are frequently with every new game started.
- Trade with neighbouring states does not significantly impact the game itself, thus failing to create a wholesome economic simulation.
So at the end of the day this game is totaly worth buying.  If you are an Indie fan then I would definetely recommend this to you, though keep in mind that I personally do not feel as if it is worth the current 12.99 EUR they are charging for it - I bought it when it was on a 50% sale - in my opinion that is more apropriate of a price.
Please continue on making similar games, I will definetely buy them and can only re-iterate that this game is equally interesting and challenging.

Great game! Doesn't require ungodly specs like so many games nowadays do, and I can comfortably run it with almost everything at the highest settings on my laptop. The gameplay is a lot of fun too, although you'll definitely want to look up some guides for the game if you are new to 2D fighters like me, as there isn't much in the way of tutorials. Sure, the 'Missions' section has tutorials of a sort that will teach you some basic combos, but I had no idea what an Advancing Guard or a Delayed Hyper Combo was until I looked it up.
Like I said though, the gameplay is way fun, and it holds true to many of the characters' abilities from their various points of origin. Zero excels at taking down large, powerful enemies with lightning fast footwork, Deadpool is silly, but quite fast and dangerous, Iron Man lacks mobility, but can fight quite well at range and in the air, and so forth. Plus, the gameplay mechanics are pretty awesome as well, such as being able to call a second or third character in to help, switching characters mid combo for more damage, or if your party is almost completely KO-ed, using your X-Factor to turn the match around and beat the snot out of your opponents with a Hyper Combo.
Overall, I'd give it a 9/10, with the only drawback being the lack of a real tutorial system.

Having played a solid 15 hours since its PC release and another 2300+ or so on console I can honestly recommend this game ONLY if you're 1) experienced with other fighting games, 2) a person who like playing a game for characters and doesn't care so much to get terribly good, or 3) a masochist.
The Good
- Huge 50 character roster full of familiar and unfamiliar faces alike from both Capcom and Marvel franchises. There's some overlap of course in terms of moveset, but every character has at least one thing that no other character does.
- Basic combos are very easy to perform while more advanced combos are satisfying to learn.
- The game is flashy and colorful, to the point that some players may even find some stage backgrounds distracting.
- Online connection is a huge improvement from the connections of the console versions.
- Getting to use multiple characters in a fight blows the door open with potenial team synergy.
- X-Factor can allow a player to either cash in on some extra early damage or go all-out for an outright comeback. It's crazy strong, but its usefulness for new players and pros alike make it a core part of the fun.
The Bad
- Low playerbase, so finding someone else to play with can be a chore.
- In higher level play, you'll stop seeing real character variety for the same ~10 or so characters, with Doom and Vergil being in particular finding themselves on most teams. This is the result of some characters having a crazy high power level in a game where all characters already have a high power level.
- Touch-of-death combos are common sights in optimized teams, making the first clean hit a huge factor in whether or not the game will be a 3v3 or a 3v2.
- Mix-ups, both in the match and incoming, can be insanely difficult to deal with if you're not familiar with them. Combined with touch-of-death combos, sometimes a player won't ever get to really play.
- Grabs are kind of whack.
- Hsien-Ko.
The Ugly
- Infinite combos. They take some practice to pull off, but that doesn't make them any more fun to watch or be subjected to.
- Again, unbalanced character roster. An individually awful character can still be made usable from a nice team comp, but this still makes a part of the roster dead weight if you want to win.
- This game will most likely never see updates from Capcom in the future, so what you see is what you get.
All in all I'd recommend this to people who love the characters or like getting broken games, in the most fun and aggrevating sense of the word.

TL;DR Good gameplay, nice length but ultimately brought down by a bad story and forgettable characters.
The game was really fun and felt like a worthy sequel to TNO and was enjoyable for the most part up until the ending. (I will be treading into spoiler territory) It unfortunately has massive sequel bait at the end. DOOM had the same problem but DOOM's focus wasnt on the story on the gameplay. This game's main draw for most of the audience was its story and it was mine too. I wanted to see how they would fight the Nazi regime out of America and how the relationships between the characters would play out further or how new characters like Grace and Super Spesh would mesh with the pre-existing cast. Sadly characters feel dumbed down and new characters are really kinda forgettable (especially Engel's daughter). Matter of fact I forgot Spesh even existed the mission after his death. Hitler's appearance felt more like a cameo or fanservice rather than a means to deepen the plot or even further it. Even the flashback sequences between BJ and his family felt like it was used purely for shock-value in some sequences and were extremely under-developed in terms of the story. Most of the cool sequences in the game were all shown in the trailers so I felt nothing new or exciting was being shown most of the time. The game also just feels like it has certain scenes for pure shock value and nothing else.
Now the ending is honestly something else. The game builds up this grand and suspense filled final act where you board Engel's ship, fight your way through it and deactivate ODIN (big security system) to help the American people. Then it happens. You get into the studio where Engel is being interviewed and are ready for a final fight, then you just press the melee key and BAM; the game is over. It builds up this big revolution in the players head and nothing ever even comes from it. You never see a revolution and the Nazis are still in America. So what was the point of the entire game? It ultimately builds up all this speed and it trips over the smallest crack and falls flat on its face in the end. I was really looking forward to this game as one of the saviours of the dying AAA single player game scene but sadly even Wolfenstein is tainted now :(

Really terrific.  Haven't tried word spud or fibbage (and lie swatter is just ok), but Drawful and YDKJ are worth the price alone.  Yes, you do want to play with your mobile phones as controllers, but it does work really well.  Had a group of seven over for a game night, and Drawful was a big hit.  YDKJ was good fun with the GF as it always is with the added benefit that we could sit back with our devices.  Good good fun.
A little more info:
YDKJ: Same as always with up to date trivia and ever increasing production values.  The best trivia game around.
Drawful: A fun pictionary type game where you are given something to draw, people submit guesses as to what it is, and then the real answer is hidden among the guesses for people to try to find.  In reality, it turns into a raucous, fun social game that runs itself seamlessly.

Fibbage and Drawful are the best party games you'll ever play, especially for a 5-8 person group. They're extremely accessible games (even the trivia/artistically challenged have a good shot at winning), as clean or dirty as the participants are willing to make them, and rounds move quickly so people at your party can rotate in and out as needed.
You Don't Know Jack 2015 is also a blast for groups of 2-4 (or by yourself)- the comedic writing has not gone downhill from the stellar 2011 entry in the series. Also the rules and question types have not changed significantly- if you liked that entry in the YDKJ series, you will also like this one.
Lie Swatter is a little underwhelming and I have yet to try Word Spud, but who cares, I can strongly recommend this game on the strength of those first three games alone. This game is an amazing value, especially compared to something like Mario Party where you're paying $50 for a game that at most 4 people can play and everyone needs a $40 controller. Here, because of the phones-as-controller thing, most people will have no problem finding enough devices for everyone to play.
I was initially hesitant about the phones-as-controllers thing because I couldn't get the provided website to work in my Windows Phone browser, but after changing a phone setting (you have to turn off Data Sense), things started working as expected and I was sold on the idea. Nobody else I've played with had any problems out of the box with their iPhones using Safari or Androids using Chrome. If some people are on cellular networks and some people are on wi-fi, the difference in latency might be noticeable in YDKJ, but it's a nonissue in Fibbage/Drawful because everyone's got plenty of time and you're not competing to press a button first.
These games are not only very technically impressive (because of the phones thing), they are also very funny and a ♥♥♥♥ing blast at parties. Buy it.

It's type of game that solid in a lot of aspects, but doesn't stand out necessarily in any way. It does a good job of putting you into the shoes of a political leader as you have to balance the different factions and their loyalty while still attempting to keep your regime going and yourself in power. There's a lot of factors that play into that, as it creates a spider's web of different factors affecting your reign over the people. But I will admit that it may not be my cup of tea, as while the simulation factor has some good elements to it, it doesn't necessarily stand out in any single way. The visuals can be awkward at times, and the UI could be clunky and has scenes that are unnecessary. The randomization element does feel realistic, but at times can be horribly punishing as your house members ask you for things that are just not feasible. There are times where the game also is inconsistent in tone and goes one step too far, where it actually starts to effect gameplay. Rogue State is a solid game, but it's hard to sit here and say that it's going to stand out. It's a title I'd target in a sale, or for those who like geo-political games.

Here are my thoughts on this game.
PROS
+ Well designed political consequences
+ WELL-BALANCED randomization
+ Thematic voice-acting
+ Polished Perspective-Animation effects
+ Multi-Genre blended well (Strategy+PoliSci+Adventure)
+ Very engaged Dev!
+ Gameplay enriching unlockables
+ Engaging Diplomacy
+ Well designed characters
+ VERY High Replayability
+ BRILLIANT title
CONS
+ Some programs seem a bit far-fetched (they are optional, so... who cares)
+ One of the randomized (possible) neighbors is very ANTI-immersion to the game's theme
+ National crest is... NOT believable, distracting!
+ Diplomacy encounters is missing vital information, making Diplomacy feel like a luck of draw
My verdict:
Outstanding! The use of retro graphics (unlike many games) is not an excuse to use for poor graphics, the graphics are very well done, with a modern use of perspective-animation, good atmospheric voice acting (A rating sound and graphics).  The gameplay is engaging, the randomization is just enough to give you a great new play each time, while maintaining the integrity of a very well designed branching plot and poli-strategy.  The unlockables for new plays are well thought out.  It is not perfect, there are certainly very unusual characters/logos in the game, which scream indie developer forcing their own pet ideas.
Very enjoyable game.

Rogue State offers a nice balance of legitimately challenging and outlandishly bizarre. As the leader of a small nation, you’ll have to make tough decisions; either run your nation as a democratically elected official or as a selfish dictator. While I wish there had been a little more, there is a surprising amount of content to be enjoyed here. Choices you wouldn’t consider important might break your career between all the nations and citizens you have to keep happy. Plus, there’s a country of sentient chickens. The game gets a couple extra points for that alone.
I’m not sure I would make a good leader. This was my thoughts as I made trade deals with the glorious nation of ‘Chickenistan’ for their goats. It comes down to communication, and I don’t speak Chicken. As my economy tanked, and my approval ratings dropped like a rock, all I could think of what how those sneaky Chickens would use my missteps to their advantage. Now, that may sound racist- but it’s actually animalist.
Rogue State is obviously a game that doesn’t take itself too seriously but does provide a difficult challenge to those who want to take a stab at being the head of state. You’re elected supreme leader of Basenji (which I guess makes you a nation of dogs) after the nation has overthrown the previous government. You’re left to decide which way you take the developing land- from dictatorship to democracy. Sure, you may want to be a liberal bastion of pot smoking hippies- but what’s to stop the other nations from steamrolling over your little drum circle?
The game has a system that looks complex at first but becomes a breeze shortly after learning the ropes. You’re able to make policy changes, such as your rules on alcohol, minimum wages, and death penalties. The more you alter them, the more you’re bound to upset one group or the other. If you approve public executions, you’ll make the nation’s ‘Patriots’ happy, but the ‘Liberals’ will not be pleased. You might want to make them happy by enforcing a livable wage, but then the ‘Captialists’ will be on your bad side. Allow businesses to run on the Sabbath, and suddenly the ‘Fundamentalists’ start sharpening their knives. Obviously, making any group happy is a hard task, and the game quickly becomes a game of “who do I want to♥♥♥♥♥♥off less?”
Since the previous party left the hall a mess, you’ll have to take your modest income and rebuild your nation. You can do this by cranking up the taxes on individuals, or trading with other nations. No matter what you do though, you don’t want to end back up in a recession- otherwise you’ll start to see even more rioting in the streets. So, do you focus on rebuilding your commerce, your education or just slap a bunch of uniforms on loyalists?
Every day begins with an event, with you needing to make a decision. It might be an oil spill off your beautiful tourist-filled beaches or a dead cabinet member, but each time you’ll have to make a decision that may destroy your reputation. You may discover that you’re building that brand new hydroelectric dam on top of an endangered species of rodents. These decisions could negatively affect either of the four main big groups and might even look bad abroad; so choose wisely. Once you start sliding, it’s hard to recover from the political tailspin.
Once you’ve built your infrastructures, laid out your policies and settled all of your trade deals, then it’s time to build your defenses. You can invest your money into soldiers, or you can dream bigger by throwing a ton of it into developing weapons of mass destruction. These choices are well designed, and usually leave you debating your morals against your self-preservation. I’d like to think we’d all try to be as altruistic as possible, but it seems the game is played best with a dash of Martin Shkreli thrown in.
Allow me to explain a little about my first shot at the big chair and how it all horribly ended. See, I tried to be very liberal on my first playthrough. Mostly Democratic- maybe a little more left-leaning than I should’ve been. With every progressive choice I made, the Fundamentalists ate me alive. Soon came the capitalists, and the Patriots; I couldn’t do anything to win any group. Tough crowd this middle-east area, am I right!?
So, after they ousted me and sent me on a plane to my own private exile, I tried again. This time, I decided to start talking out of both sides of my mouth. This strategy worked well for a short time, but after awhile I found out that it really didn’t work any better. I told the other nations around me that I hated America (kinda weird that the USA is the only vilified outside nation), that I didn’t trust the United Nations and that we shouldn’t ignore the ‘Old Ways’. Then, when it came to policy, I simply voted down the middle of the road. I guess that made me a do-nothing president, because despite my excellent 90% approval rating, my army suddenly left me. I was quickly attacked by another nation, who wanted all of my money. I agree to the extortion, and shortly after a rebellion overthrew me. Those damn Chickens; I gave them a hell of a deal for our electronics, and they sat back and did nothing.
Outside of that, there’s not much more to this game than your main office and the war room. The game does do a great job of creating the impression that there’s a whole land outside of your little building, so it does feel larger than the three screens you’ll see. Every decision you would think you could make is here, and it should provide a nice distraction if the prospect interests you.
I guess in closing, I imagine it’s a good thing I’ve never thought about running for a political office because I’m awful at it. Simply awful. At least this game allowed me to have fun with that knowledge, and I learned a lot about my laurels in the face of trying to appease my voters. I enjoyed my experience with the game, and I would recommend it to anyone with illusions of grandeur. Rogue State requires a nice balance of loyalty and fabrication and an ability to balance several different groups; that is if you don’t want to end up like the last guy.

Though lacking a considerable amount of polish (bare-bones main menu, no foreseeable way to exit a game in progress), there are a considerable number of moving parts here that work together to emulate the feeling of running a sovereign state. At first blush, the mechanics and choices feel simple and one dimensional, but as the game progresses, you realized there is a lot to consider.
At it's core, it feels like being a world leader from Civ V, but all of the changes you effect come from your office. I can see a history, politics, or model UN buff going crazy for this game.
For the lack of production value, $12.99 might be a bit high, but considering how niche the game is, it might be the only way for you to get that political fix.

It really turned out to be a pretty big disappointment.
I guess it is somewhat supposed to be a "rogue-like" strategy game, but the game seems to randomly punish you, even in the first few turns, which can basically ruin a play through. A lot of the game's strategy seems to be based on guesswork, such as how other countries' leaders will respond to your talking points. Also, factions seem to randomly hate you or like you for no obvious reasons, even though you haven't changed policies whatsoever. Too many turns, I found myself with basically nothing to do and just skipping to the next turn. Maintaining even a half-way decent military is virtually impossible, and actually gaining enough intelligence to use that military well is equally impossible, as it takes huge amounts of money to do either.
Overall, this game basically presents you with an enormous mountain to climb, and gives you absolutely none of the tools necessary to even begin to remotely even consider climbing it. It has generally just been a terrible, frustrating experience to play. It's basically Torchlight.  Skill trees, HP and mana, a pet, color coded loot, etc.
Some highlights:
Skills have powerups you can enable per use that are fueled by a third resource called rage.  These do things like more damage, more targets, heal you on hit, and similar bonuses. You get rage when you kill monsters.  It's a nice little system I wouldn't mind seeing elsewhere.
Easy respec on abilities and skills.  This was great for me when I realized investing heavily in the first skill wasn't a good long term solution, and when I realized one of my passives wasn't needed anymore.  You can also refund some of the starting skills if they aren't useful for you.   You can't respec perks for some reason, so check a guide before investing. Some of the late-game ones are straight out better than the early ones.
Some meh-lights:
The writing I found to be adequate.  Nothing exceptional, but it didn't pain me.
The core combat started out kind of bleh.  Slow, low damage attacks and limited mana.  It picked up after a little while, but the start wasn't great.  When I got the laser skill, it was just as fun as it was in Torchlight.
I started to get some loot fatigue near the end.  There's a lot of items, and even with the summary tooltips it's sometimes hard to parse which item is really better.
One downer:
A certain boss is one of the more frustrating bosses I've faced in a diablo-like.  He has a charge attack that could one-hit me, and he would do it from offscreen so I had no chance to dodge.  He also had homing missiles and infinite ranged attack mooks.  I did not enjoy that fight at all.

Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare had one of the largest impacts on the way FPS games are created today, and it just so happens that it is one of my most favorite games of all time.
While the newer entries into the Call of Duty franchise have become rather stale, Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare still holds it's own as one of the best games in the series. With an awesome singleplayer campaign, focused on the life of a new SAS recruit and Marine Force Recon member, to a multiplayer experience that never seems to grow stale (even after a total amount of 40 days played across multiple platforms), you will not feel underwhelmed with content.
The campaign is one of my most favorite aspects of this game. After multiple Veteran playthroughs, I can say the game brings a decent enough challenge to your average gamer, and will keep collectors busy while in search of all 32 intel locations. And those who like a decent storyline in their FPS games, you will be catered to aswell. Difficulty spikes are also few and far between throughout the campaign, so you will not be overly frustrated.
Now, to the most popular part of any Call of Duty or any other FPS, the multiplayer. Being the first in the series to implement RPG based aspects such as customization and perks, it may seem like there's much less than the newer games, but don't let that throw you off. While it may have fewer perks and customizable options, you don't feel overwhelmed with options of attatchments you may never use, and all perks have a purpose. All attatchments and camos are unlocked through regular kills and headshots, which I really miss from the new entries into the franchise.
Even today, closing in on Spring of 2014, almost 7 years after it's releease, the multiplayer still has quite a few open servers, and a great amount of people playing, and no one should have trouble finding a server under 150 ping, which was one of my major concerns before purchasing this game on PC.
The verdict concludes that Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare has withstood the test of technological time, and still leads as one of the best FPS games ever created. With an oustanding singleplayer campaign, and endless multiplayer experience, I recommend everyone who loves FPS games purchase this as soon as possiible.

I am not a big review writer. The fact that i deem it necessary for this game is due to it being one of the best games I ever played. Still got the feels in me, so this probably won't be very objective (but I'll try)!
Ori and the Blind Forest is a story-driven action platformer which really lives from and for its atmosphere.
First, there's the visuals. The developers have put a lot of love and work in the graphics/art. Everything looks and feels right, from the beautiful artwork to the fluent movements of the character and foes. The combination of 2D and 3D works very well, the effects are nicely done and well designed for Oris different abilites.
The soundtrack is, simply said, stunning, providing you with a nice musical background during the normal gameplay while becoming more present and driven when it counts. I mean "Great Soundtrack" is even part of the tags for this game!
While the graphics and sound are already good, it's the gameplay that really counts for me when playing a game. And this platformer does everything right. The level design is spot-on. You travel through one continuous world, no loading, no fade-outs, unlocking new areas by gaining abilities or progressing in the story which often changes certain parts of the map. Said abilities can be found throughout the world and the game does a good job in "leading" you to them when the time is right. Additionally to the abilities you can gain certain passive and active skills by leveling which adds even more depth to the gameplay.
The controls are precise and thought out (on gamepad). I always had full control over Oris movement, so I always knew it was MY fault when you fell into another bottomless pit or some nasty spikes.
The difficulty was good for me, challenging yet fair.
I especially liked the saving system. You can save the game by placing a "soul portal" which costs energy (like mana). Energy is also needed for certain doors and a special attack, so you have to choose wisely when and where to save!
The impact of the story can be summarized in a simple "'dem feels...".
I'd recommend this game to anyone who doesn't outright HATE platformers, tears, cute stuff and try'n'error.

The game was really fun and felt like a worthy sequel to TNO and was enjoyable for the most part up until the ending. This game's main draw for most of the audience was its story and it was mine too. I wanted to see how they would fight the Nazi regime out of America and how the relationships between the characters would play out further or how new characters like Grace and Super Spesh would mesh with the pre-existing cast. Sadly characters feel dumbed down and new characters are really kinda forgettable (especially Engel's daughter). Matter of fact I forgot Spesh even existed the mission after his death. Hitler's appearance felt more like a cameo or fanservice rather than a means to deepen the plot or even further it. Even the flashback sequences between BJ and his family felt like it was used purely for shock-value in some sequences and were extremely under-developed in terms of the story. Most of the cool sequences in the game were all shown in the trailers so I felt nothing new or exciting was being shown most of the time. The game also just feels like it has certain scenes for pure shock value and nothing else.
Now the ending is honestly something else. The game builds up this grand and suspense filled final act where you board Engel's ship, fight your way through it and deactivate ODIN (big security system) to help the American people. Then it happens. You get into the studio where Engel is being interviewed and are ready for a final fight, then you just press the melee key and BAM; the game is over. It builds up this big revolution in the players head and nothing ever even comes from it. You never see a revolution and the Nazis are still in America. So what was the point of the entire game? It ultimately builds up all this speed and it trips over the smallest crack and falls flat on its face in the end. I was really looking forward to this game as one of the saviours of the dying AAA single player game scene but sadly even Wolfenstein is tainted now :(

Trine is an absolutely incredible game. In this review, I will list the many things I loved about it and the few things I disliked.
Pros:
1) The graphics are absolutely gorgeous. They're extremely colorful  and detailed.
2) The abilities of the characters are well thought out, and you are rewarded for looking for chests.
3) The mechanics of the three characters work very well together. Near the end of the game, I was finding myself subconsciously switching from one character to another.
Cons:
1) The characters would occasionally glitch out, especially while using the Theif's grapple.
2) Enemies were not developed well. Much of the time, a skeleton trying to attack me would begin running and swinging at a wall. Took away from the immersion and flow of gameplay.
3) Bosses were not made well. [SPOILER ALERT] I had to face the same two bosses twice. I defeated the first one, then the second one, then I had to face the first one again, and the second one again. These were the only bosses (excluding the final boss). Also, as I was fighting with them, they glitched out. The second/fourth boss froze during battle and let me kill him.
4) The story of the game was short and undeveloped. I'm still rather confused about the plot of the game. If most games create a story and base the game off the story, it seems like Trine made the game and then wrote the story afterwards. I would've liked more character development/attatchment. As well, the story itself didn't last long. I beat the game in 6.9 hours, which included me gathering nearly every experience bottle and chest in every map.
5) The end of the game was not satisfying whatsoever. [SPOILER ALERT] The final boss isn't a fight. You must climb through a level rapidly, fighting skeletons and destroying objects dropped on you with the boss. In the end, you climb onto a platform with the 3 artifacts, and you win. Then, during a cutscene, the "boss" tries to attack the theif, and gets crushed in one hit by the Knight's hammer. This wasn't satisfying at all, the battle was intense enough but the end left me feeling cheated out of something, like I still needed to finish the battle.
All-in-all, this game would be absolutely astounding if the developers were more thorough. Whether this was due to a low budget, time limitations, or lazy development, the game felt incomplete. I recommend buying this game and playing it if you're looking for some fun. I hope the next two games will be better developed, and if you plan on playing those, I highly suggest playing this first to get even a vague idea of what the story is about.

I thought about writing a long, extensive review describing the gameplay and story details of this game. I thought about describing the emotional ups and downs of a story that really touched me and made me appreciate the fact that videogames have become a medium for sharing poignant and moving tales.
Eventually, I decided that the only thing that needs to be said is that this is an experience that you have to take for yourself.
Yes, this is a RPGMaker game, and it is arguably the most beautifully artistic and sonorous one you will play.
Yes, there is no actual RPG gameplay in this and is essentially a walking simulator at its most basic, but those would just be distractions from the main message.
Yes, it is really short, but that just means it conveys what it needs to tell in the most compact and meaningful way possible.
Really, just try it. Having someone else describing it for you, I feel, ruins the experience. I can't guarantee that you will necessarily like it, but I believe that, at least subconsciously, it will get you to think and feel how wonderful and powerful emotions can be and how deeply they can affect you.

Being the giant trivia nerd that I am (I attend trivia at a local bar nearly every week), I was eager to try the video game version of the You Don't Know Jack party game. I had heard positive buzz about the game and that it combined good trivia questions with excellent writing and a silly sense of humor, which I found to be true. I saw the 2015 edition of the You Don't Know Jack game on a steep sale in the Steam store, but it came bundled with a bunch of other games from the You Don't Know Jack developers. I wanted to play You Don't Know Jack and figured the other games were probably just throw away titles that the developers shoved in with You Don't Know Jack, but I was pleasantly surprised to be mostly wrong. This will be a bit of an unusual review since I'll be covering five games at once, but I'll try to give my opinion on the package of games as a whole and then some quick thoughts on each game in the package.
Each of the games in the Jackbox Party Pack assumes that all players in the room have either a smartphone or tablet or laptop or some other internet-enabled device. Each player uses their internet device, usually a smartphone, to connect to a web app and enter a "room code" which links the game together with the other devices and players in the room. Depending on which game in the pack you're playing, each player will submit either answers to questions, or drawings or whatever data is required for the game through their smartphone. I was actually quite surprised and impressed with how responsive the web app was when submitting data from my phone. There was almost no delay at all. It's a kind of neat strategy of utilizing the smartphones people likely already have as input devices and displaying the other game information on the main TV screen. I hope to see more party games integrate with smartphones since it's often hard to play video games with really large groups of people since controllers are usually limited.
You Don't Know Jack 2015 Edition
Likely the most recognizable game in the pack, You Don't Know Jack 2015 edition was the first game I played. It was pretty much exactly what I was expecting: good trivia questions delivered with silly humor. I thought the humor was a little hit and miss. When the writing was funny, it was funny. But when the jokes didn't land, they definitely did not land. The trivia questions were difficult, but still fair. If you weren't too familiar with the question category, I found it kind of hard to contribute since the game penalizes you for wrong answers. But if you like trivia and enjoy questions delivered with a crude sense of humor, you'll enjoy You Don't Know Jack
Fibbage
If you've ever played the party game Balderdash, you'll find Fibbage very familiar. In Fibbage, you're presented an incomplete sentence about weird fact and it's up to you to fill in the blank. Then everyone's answers are displayed on screen and you have to guess which is the actual true answer. You usually want to try to be as tricky as possible answer submissions, since points are awarded if your opponents guess your false answer as the correct one.
Drawful
Probably my favorite game in the pack, Drawful is pretty much the same concept as Fibbage, but with drawings. You'll be given a wacky subject that you'll have to make a drawing of. Once your drawing is complete, it's displayed on screen for all to see. Your opponents have to come up with fake answers for the title of your drawing while also trying to figure out what your drawing is actually about. There's a lot of fun to be had with this one, since the names of the drawings given to you are often crazy. Then add in the fact that all players are drawing on their phones with their fingers. This results in the drawings usually ending up being totally ridiculous. Then guessing who made what with your friends and figuring out what the real titles are while sifting out the hilarious fake title submissions is a great recipe for fun.
Word Spud
This one's fun, but you'll probably only play it once or twice. You'll be given a starting word, then a randomly selected player has to make a compound word or phrase from the initial word by adding another word. For example, the starting word might be "Video", to which a player might add "Game". Then another random player would be given "Game" and be expected to add another word to it. After each submission, all players can vote on whether to accept or reject the new word. If the word is accepted, the chain continues, otherwise a new random word is generated. The fun here is thinking quickly to come up with words to complete a clever or funny phrase. At the end of the game, which usually lasts a few minutes or so, Word Spud will show you your entire word chain which when read out loud is usually worth a few laughs.
Lie Swatter
Probably the weakest game in the pack, lie swatter presents a true/false trivia question and awards points for the most correct answers. This is probably the most simple and least creative game in the pack, but it's also playable by up to 100 people at a time, so this might be the way to go if you have a really large group of people.
Summary
I've been having a really great time with the Jackbox Party Pack. It's great to put up on the TV when I have more people over than I do controllers for traditional video games. You Don't Know Jack is fun for when you want to show off your random knowledge while being amused with crude jokes. Drawful was the surprise hit of the pack for me, easily providing hours of hilarious entertainment. Fibbage and Word Spud are midly enteraining, while Lie Swatter felt like a shoe-in. But if you often host large-ish groups of people (5-8) and are looking for video games to play, I would still highly recommend the Jackbox Party Pack

Showered with my dad, 10/10.
Did I do Steam reviews right? I think I did.
ANYWAY, Shower With Your Dad Simulator 2015: Do You Still Shower With Your Dad is actually a good game. I certainly know when I see a game with "Simulator" in the title, I immediately think that it's going to be garbage, but after watching Jim Sterling's  15 minute YouTube video on it, I was compelled to buy it.
The premise is that you're one of three little boys, looking to take a shower with the correct father. When it first starts, you simply move over to the correct father and it's incredibly easy. However, once you really get going, they actually start to get challenging: various hazards are introduced (such as water puddles, which makes you move uncontrollably), 'slippery when wet' sign (which get knocked over and slow your pace down to a crawl), or even the curtains in the shower being pulled after the initial second the dads materialize.
In addition to various curveballs being thrown at you, there are an impressive amount of different game modes, which range from changing your character (and therefore the dad you need) after every successful match, to a Flappy Birds clone, where you're in a bath tub attempting to save 69 of your dads (and after completing the mode, apparently your dad is the president of the US...?). There are also various unlocks that you get after playing so long, such as soap (which doubles your score for a set amount of time), a razor that removes  the dads' hair (making it more difficult to figure out which dad you need), etc. Nearly every time I thought to myself "well, I've had enough of this game for now", I've unlocked a new game mode or item or something that incentivized me to keep playing just a bit longer.
Although I've only played about an hour and a half of the game, I've been impressed by the game. I hate to bring up the subject because it's different for everyone, but I'm completely happy with paying $0.99 for an hour and a half of amusing content, especially so since I'm naturally drawn to weird, silly games. If this game was any more than $2.50 I can't say I could recommend it, but a dollar is the right amount, I feel.
I don't want to give it an actual numerical score, so instead I'll just say this: do you like weird games? If so, take a chance on Shower With Your Dad Simulator 2015: Do You Still Shower With Your Dad. If you aren't at least interested by the title of the game, well, odds are you won't enjoy the game.

"It's a weird game, it's a niche game and it's a very very chill game."
That's what Sean Murray wrote in his last post on the NMS site before the game was released, and it's still the most accurate description. It may be the kind of weird that many people don't like, too niche for the average gamer, or chill in a way that some people find boring, but if you give it a chance you may be surprised to find it's the kind of game you never knew you wanted.
I've recently realised that it has become my favourite game, and even though I sometimes need a long break from it when things start to feel stale, I always come back and end up losing many nights of sleep to it. It doesn't have a big learning curve, which makes jumping back in even after months of absence really easy and is one of the reasons it's such a chill experience.
If you wait for adventure to find you without putting any effort into it, it might never come and you could end up hating everything this game chooses to be.
There are no conventional quests, which sometimes means you need a sense of imagination and willingness to set your own goals. (
Quests have been added to the game now.) It doesn't tell you how to play or force you on a set path. Everyone's journey is different.
You could dedicate dozens of hours to discovering the lore or completely ignore it in favour of hunting down pirates. Set course for the center of the galaxy or settle down and build a base in one of the many community-made hubs. Become a zoologist and make it into the Hall of Fame for discovering the largest aquatic creature. Assemble the prettiest collection of pink starships. Plant a farm of space weed and become rich. The universe is your playground.
NMS is a large canvas with endless possibilities for expansion. It's been great to see it evolve over the past year. I admire Hello Games for not giving up on their dream and their community despite the backlash they had to endure, and can't wait to see what they have in store for us next.

Every webzine is praising this game, even Rock Paper Shotgun which I trust almost blindly.
Well this time I have to disagree.
Wolfenstein 2: The New Colossus has a great start for which it will be remembered for some time. The way it delves into the main character past is something unexpected and strong. I admit I was moved to tears at one particular flashback, even if the whole game is about shooting and axing other people in the face.
Now, how does it compare to The New Order? Well, it's not that different, in fact the formula is always the same: a dual wielding semi-stealth corridor shooter. Nothing is improved from the first one and I feel like Machine Games played it too safe. The gunplay is fast paced and satisfiying indeed, but I expected some new mechanics to enhance the experience. The sound effects, voice actors and music are great while the graphic is pretty good. Gory I would say :) It's nice that the enemies bloody corpses remain on the map and don't disappear, it gives you a sense of massacre which is what Terror Billy is good at.
And the STORY? I've read that the developer focused on the story telling and single player experience. Well this is true for the first half of the game, but for the second half...
It's where everything crumbles down to a big NOTHING. Just when things get interesting the game ENDS. It just ends. No boss fights, no climatic face off with the antagonist... Nope. It cuts rapidly to the ending, making a 59.99 game way too short. Sure there are the Enigma Machine missions but they are all the same: enter an already visited area, kill commander. Not good, repetetive and honestly quite boring.
Dear Machine Games... This is really STUPID. A complete letdown. I know everybody is complaining about characters like Grace, but that's not the problem. The problem is the game ends so abrouptly that there isn't even TIME to start liking them. They appear and after two or three missions the game is OVER. Roll credits, stupid djent cover of Twisted Sister - We're Not Gonna Take it and... DLC? C'mon, they even put a mysterious object in the plot, something that could probably open up the story to something mystical or extraterrestrial, only to reveal that it's just a DOOR KNOB. So lazy.
To make it even worse, the main villain Frau Engel is one of the most cruel and sadistic ever seen in a game and then... You don't get too fight her. You just SLAY her like a normal enemy. Ok, I can see the "genious" here, she is nothing special afterall, just another white supremacist and so she gets to die like any other one of them. That would have been cool, in a MOVIE. Not in a VIDEOGAME.
I loved The New Order, it was one of the best FPS I've played in recent years (only beaten by DOOM) and believe me, I've been playing and loving this genre since Wolfenstein 3D and the first Doom came out :) So I am a bit conflicted, I'd like to recommend this game, but not at this price. For now I'll go with a NO, even if I want to specify that it's not a bad game, but it will let you down just when things start to get good.
I hope this "fashion" of making HALF games at full prices stops. Learn from Naughty Dog for crying out loud!
Review UPDATE: I am re-playing The New Order for the tenth time, just to see how it compares to The New Colossus and... Holy macaroni, how did they screw up the sequel so badly??? I'd like to think it was "rushed", but then again the DOOM campaign was awesome and complete, even if the game had the multiplayer part in it, so I don't think it is the publisher fault, not this time. I have just checked now and there is already a SEASON PASS of 29,99 bucks of three separate episodes where there isn't even BJ!

The Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing is one of the best ARPG I've ever played. Why?
Let's start with the graphics. It looks beautiful. In my opinion, it's the best looking ARPG I've ever played. Finally some ARPG that overcome Titan Quest in this part. The soundtrack is also very good.
I also like the enviroment. The game takes place in a country called Borgovia. It's similiar to the one you've seen in the original Van Helsing film. The nature and the village you will visit seems to be inspired by medieval Hungary and Romania. In most of the cases, the enemies you will face in the country will be monsters- wolves, spiders, but also Rusalka, a beast from Slavic myths. The situation will change once you enter the capital city, Borgova. The city contains more steampunk elements, e.g. robot soldiers or mutants, than the countryside. Some of the buildings there are inspired by buildings from our world.
What I like the most about this games is the humour. In addition to the easter eggs, the dialogs between your character and Katarina are also well written and amusing.
There is also a tower defence minigame. In this minigame, three waves of enemies would like to get into your base and you must stop them. In order to do that, you can put traps on the way to your lair. It can be a platform that will activate once an enemy will step on it. Or you can place various towers next to the path leading to your base. And of course, you and Katarina will also take place in preventing your enemies to get there.
What I don't like very much is the fact that skills needs mana and they also have cooldown time after you've used them. I think it is not necessary. If you ask me, I believe that only one of those should be used. I would rather use only mana, like it is done in Torchlight. And also the fact that you can shoot enemies that are below or above you is not very good, in my opinion.

The Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing Complete Pack is a beautiful, isometric action-rpg that provides a challenging experience which has a sense of humor, an interesting companion system, satisfying combat, very buggy controller support, and some noteworthy differences from the base version.
There's a lot of quirky referential humor in the game that I do not want to spoil here. Just make sure to explore everywhere and talk to everyone and... everything, especially in the first town. The world is not grim dark; it has a joke or two up its sleeve.
Katarina, Van Helsing's companion, is very helpful and has very interesting ways to alter her behavior to fit your play style. She will level up with you and has her own set of skills, two with the DLC. You can also choose three different states for her which include ghost (peaceful), melee, and ranged. You can alter how aggressive she is with enemies. She can also pick up different items of varying rarities automatically according to player desires. I had her pick up all the gold, ignore the white items, pick up the magic items, and fight enemies in melee form. It is a neat feature that is greatly appreciated and should be present in more games with companions/followers.
The combat requires you to pay attention and engage its systems if success interests you. The game has a combo system that alters how a skill can be used. For example, Earthquake, a spell that deals damage in a line, has three different power-ups that can be used in a combo: Brutal Stomp which adds 1.5 meters to the skill's width, Intense Shockwave which adds 30% more damage, and Scorching Fumes which burns everything hit for 10% of Van Helsing's Spellpower. You can spend skill points on the ones you want and organize them in whatever order. You stack up to three combos with the a, s, and d keys resulting in a very powerful skill waiting to be used. I went with 90% additional damage for Earthquake with a high critical chance build to great effect. I could have gone with 1.5 meters to width and 60% additional damage. Other skills have different power-ups available for experimentation. You will be working with Katarina to dispose of monsters while using tricks to change the flow of battle. I often used the one that freezes time to give myself a chance to observe the situation and line up Earthquake perfectly, especially when fighting extremely large groups.
This game will test the average player's abilities, but the systems it has in place makes it forgiving and approachable. Despite dying a good dozen or so times during my time with the game, I only had to pay a bit of gold to resurrect and continue the battle against evil. There are also special npcs in towns that can refund skill points for both the player and Katarina should you want to try a different build or made a mistake in your allocations.
Do not use a controller with this game. Playing this game with a controller resulted in a frustrating battle with the user interface. Looking at the skill power-ups wouldn't work for skills at the bottom of the page and laying down certain traps did not turn out very well. The combat experience works well enough, but the UI problems are severe enough to just stick with mouse and keyboard. The UI for mouse and keyboard results in faster interactions for everything and lets you properly look at all the information available. I spent fifteen hours with this game using the controller until I finally decided to stop torturing myself. The last four hours were blissful.
Finally, the complete pack comes with three different pieces of DLC which includes an additional skill tree for Katarina known as Blue Blood and two more classes, Thaumaturge and Arcane Mechanic. The Blue Blood tree has some really powerful abilities that drastically change Katarina's performance. She could rival me in power and I do not know what I would have done without her. Blue Blood allows for major damage, health, and defense increases. It also gives her different passive spells that she can activate based on chance or even death for one of them (big explosion). It even adds an often used Trick called Ghostly Mirage which allows for two Katarina illusions that can deal damage. The two extra classes, basically a mage and a scientist/engineer, have one main skill tree and a heavily modified Tricks tree allowing for a different experience from the Hunter who wields swords and/or pistols with some magic. If the classes do not interest you, I still heavily recommend Blue Blood unless you want an extra challenging experience.
The Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing is a good action-rpg that should entertain those familiar with the genre. Again, I am heavily recommending to not use a controller with this game.

As someone who simply adores the genre while simultaneously sucking at almost every game in said genre, Skullgirls is easily my favorite fighting game to date. The mechanics feel great, the art and music are to die for, every character is fun to play as, and pulling off tricky, high-damage combos feels incredibly satisfying. Bonus points awarded for having a tutorial that teaches you more about how to play fighting games, rather than just Skullgirls itself. If you like fighting games or have any interest in getting into them, Skullgirls is definitely a solid choice.
That being said, fighting games are a hard genre to get into. You have to accept that you're going to lose pretty much every single match you play online for a while. It will sting pretty hard when you find yourself beaten over and over, but you need to take those losses as lessons. "What part of my character could I make better use of?" "Do I need to work on my footsie game?" "What would my opponent do if I tried this on them?" Fighting games are like intricate games of chess; half of the game is execution, while the other half is mind games - knowing what your opponent is going to do next. Try looking up some tutorials, or even tournament footage to get ideas on what you can improve upon. If you're willing to put in the work to git gud, then you're going to find fighting games are one of the most exciting video game genres around.

Large world, tons of things to do, a variety of skill trees – Fallout 3 is a good rpg if all you want to do is (slowly) wander and explore. The repetitive quests and drab scenery quickly bore. Bethesda doesn’t give a damn about the game, and hasn’t patched it in years;
is REQUIRED to play the game without constant crashing (seriously, Bethesda? Wtf). Those curious to see what the franchise is all about should check out Fallout: New Vegas, it’s the better game.
Total size on my hard-drive (GOTY): 9 GB
+ Good character skill tree and humorously labeled perks.
+ Great ambient soundtrack by Inon Zur - though by default the music volume is turned extremely low for some reason.
+ Great world design. A wasteland filled with rubble, mostly, but there’s just enough left standing to provide a hint of a glorious pre-nuclear, 1950s America.
+ Quick-saving or manually saving saves your character wherever they are standing. Checkpoints are present too, but it’s getting rare to have a game save your actual location.
+/-  Decent story. However, while story progression is not level-locked, you HAVE to level via side-quests and exploratory looting if you don’t want to die dozens of times.
+/-  Healthy modding scene, though the required mod-managers are sometimes glitchy.
+/ - Graphically decent for its age – the trees in Oasis are impressively leafy and the water in the canals has a nice reflection – but the overall palette has too many browns and greys. I understand that it is a post-nuclear landscape, and all major life has been killed or altered, but some variety would be nice. (There are mods that can help with this.)
- A community-made patch is required to play the game without crashing. It’s not even a large file – around 1 MB. Why couldn’t Bethesda just patch the game?
- Poorly optimized. Micro-stutter any time a new area streamed in. Yes, I have an Intel cpu (i5-4590). No, the gameplay was not stutter-free.
- Walking simulator. I hope you enjoy desolate scenery, because you’ll have a lot of time to stare at it.
- Re-used NPC character models.
- No hotkeys. You’ll be constantly tabbing into the Pip-boy wrist-tablet-thingy just to swap weapons (if you run out of ammo for one weapon, you switch to bare fists until you equip another weapon. Not very good in a firefight). Inventory management, stats, game map, local map – it’s all in the Pip-boy. It fits the world-concept, but it’s annoying as hell.
- The most effective character builds require focused specialization. This hurts the ability to vary approaches and tactics.
- It is possible to short-circuit the story by stumbling across a vault you shouldn’t access until later.
- The characters of the wasteland would be more interesting if they gave you more than fetch-quests. “If you want information that I have, you need to go to X and get me three Y’s!” People complain about fetch-quests dominating open-world games today, but look to the past; fetch quests were there.
- Combat gets boring fast. Use VATS (Vault-Tec Assisted Targeting System) until it runs out. Start backing up, throwing mines or grenades while waiting for VATS to recharge (shooting guns without VATS just wastes bullets). Then use VATS again.
- Horrible shooting mechanics (outside of VATS, that is). I could pour an entire clip of bullets into an armorless mutant, but his health bar won’t budge – even though he is mere feet away, swinging a sledgehammer at my head, and my aiming reticule was red the entire time.
-
might have trouble targeting enemies without VATS, but enemies have perfect accuracy from a hundred meters away – sometimes scoring hits before they’re even visible on the minimap.
- Hidden walls. For all of Fallout 3’s open world reputation, there are hidden walls in unexpected places – and quite often, too.
- Occasionally poor fast-travel, which can teleport you into the middle of a group of enemies, resulting in near-immediate death.
A “meh” verdict for Fallout 3; there’s things to like for sure. Usually that means a “thumbs up with reservations” verdict because, while I subjectively didn’t like it, there’s no point in giving a thumbs down to a working game that didn’t click for me. But Fallout 3, as it downloads from Steam, is not playable. That’s enough to flip my verdict to “not recommended.” Users shouldn’t have to download and install mods to play the game they paid for. Don’t bother with Fallout 3.

Initial Comments Prior to V1.3 See below for updated comments
I played this game the on its initial release, stopped playing it, and then tried the updated content in the last two weeks.
First of all, many of the initial poor reviews related to features players expected to see in the content but never made it into the game. However, from the very beginning, I never expected multiplayer. I understand the language between a shared "world" idea and in game player interactions. As such, I am not giving this game a negative review because of the lack of multiplayer.
Pros:
Based on game play and reviews of the game code by experts, the game does have a great engine with potential for the limitless variety that Sean Murray claimed.
Overall I find the gameplay to be smooth and the FPS fine.
It does deliver a large universe where you do go to planets that no other player has visited.
Cons
Vegetation size, in particular, trees, is extremely limited and as such really limits the variety of the planets. They quickly begin to feel like more of the same thing.
The updated content is especially buggy. The base building features a variety of fetch quests but they are so buggy you have to either delete building parts or start the base over again multiple times to actually complete the quests and get the rewards which are required gear updates.
The challenges HG faced with producing the game are widely documented and can forgive some problems and even what amounted to an alpha release last summer. However, there is no logical explanation for releasing updates frought with bugs. There are many small develop teams producing excellent products and this cannot dismiss the shortcomings of this game. Empyrion and 7 days to die are far superior games and both are still in alpha.
The addition of survival mode did take a step in the correct direction; however, the dangers are still too limited. The AI for all drones is limited and it leads to a flat combat experience. It would be better without combat at all rather than deliver a subpar experience. Initially Hello Games advertised the game to be like a sci fi novel. The problem is that sci fi adventure is only as engaging as the dangers the player faces whether combat or environmental. There is no danger here.
The key bindings for PC are a mess. Some controls you can rebind but others you cannot. If you are a left handed player, you better learn how to use right handed controls. I assume this works well for console but it just does not meet the standard for a PC game.
While the addition of exocraft is interesting, the design of the planets do not really make these vehicles fun to use. I found them so annoying in terms of getting stuck, I preferred to walk and use the jet pack.
The base building is a mere shadow of other games in the genre and really offers very little functionality in the game. The game's strength is moving to new systems and visiting new planets until you are bored. Bases do not fit in with the games exploration concept.
One of the advertised methods of play was to be a trader; however, the only main trading most players are doing in the game now is farming at their base and selling the items at the nearest station. The galaxy map is so aweful with its navagation that finding to previous systems or even keeping track of where you want to go is nearly impossible. You should be able to rotate the galaxy map and mouse over stars to see if you have been there before. You can use a free exploration mode but the way that you move your cursor to see the system details is one of the most frustrating game mechanics I have ever had to try and deal with.
There is praise here for HG building their own engine and really doing it well, but the content the player is visual left with and the variety of bugs and mechanical issues are too many with such little actual game content.
For those players who played in Sep like I did and are considering going back to the game, it is a really bad idea. Many resources we could harvest at launch now require new mods and the only way to get them is to suffer through the buggy fetch quests.
I had hoped given time HG could salvage this game into something special but the persistent content issues suggest there is no hope for this game. The developers would be better off to abandon this mess and take a good engine to a new project.
OVERALL REVIEW CHANGED V1.3 Updated Review
Many of my issues with previous versions have been corrected by the devs and it appears they are going to continue to improve the game.
Improvements Include:
Better visuals
More variety in everything from planets, animals and flora, and ships - some ships even look alien now
Quests are working much better than previously. Some people with old saves have reported issues but there are current solutions for most problems
The story is engaging and the length is comparable to other AAA games' stories
Galatic Map and UI is greatly improved
Flight and space battles are improved - however it is not a flight simulator and it never will be
Work is being done for "joint exploration" although exactly what that will include is not yet quite clear but since I never expected MP or Coop, I am not much concerned about it.
Lingering Issues
With all new updates, there are some bugs that have to be fixed but HG has already released some fixes so they are actively working on it.
One criticism is that I would have liked to see fewer content related bugs for the launch of 1.3. I cant say this is an HG specific complaint but I would like to see a bit more testing before release.

As someone who simply adores the genre while simultaneously sucking at almost every game in said genre, Skullgirls is easily my favorite fighting game to date. The mechanics feel great, the art and music are to die for, every character is fun to play as, and pulling off tricky, high-damage combos feels incredibly satisfying. Bonus points awarded for having a tutorial that teaches you more about how to play fighting games, rather than just Skullgirls itself. If you like fighting games or have any interest in getting into them, Skullgirls is definitely a solid choice.
That being said, fighting games are a hard genre to get into. You have to accept that you're going to lose pretty much every single match you play online for a while. It will sting pretty hard when you find yourself beaten over and over, but you need to take those losses as lessons. "What part of my character could I make better use of?" "Do I need to work on my footsie game?" "What would my opponent do if I tried this on them?" Fighting games are like intricate games of chess; half of the game is execution, while the other half is mind games - knowing what your opponent is going to do next. Try looking up some tutorials, or even tournament footage to get ideas on what you can improve upon. If you're willing to put in the work to git gud, then you're going to find fighting games are one of the most exciting video game genres around.

Hello reistance fighters,
Normally, I do not write many reviews, but regarding the many negative backlash the game gets, I feel like I need to give an objective and unbias opinion on it.
I`ve just finished the main story. I made the mistake of reading the mostly negative reviews of people who the first 1-2 days after launch. They made me doubt my previous decision to preorder the game. After all, I loved the last Wolfenstein title. Back then, I did not expect too much from a Wolfenstein fame – and I was proven wrong. The game was great! So, I was concerned by how negative the reviews for the sequel were – people complaining about everything, asking for refunds.
After finally finishing the game, I CAN NOT relate to the negative reactions, at all. Let me share a few impressions:
Graphics: The graphics are amazing. The game is superbly optimized for PC. It looks and runs perfect. On an old i7 4th gen. and a RX480, the game runs with 120fps at 1200p, in MY LIFE ultra-preset. Few other games can deliver such polish. Sure, there are some muddy textures used here and there, but with full intention and with performance in mind. If you do not look for them, you will never see any. Graphics are stellar – period.
Sound: Voice acting is again great. Details are present everywhere, from squeaking hulls to enemies chatting. The soundtrack is very good, again. Sure, not exactly what you would expect from a WWII shooter, but this is Wolfenstein! Weapons sound good to me – powerful and fun. Sure, it`s not BF1, but who cares, when you can blow Nazis to pieces in so many visually spectacular ways?
Story: The story is as good and as interesting as the previous one – whatever this means. The antagonist – Frau Engel – is a brutal and disturbing advisory. Characters are well interesting and there are many trivial things and Easter-eggs hidden throughout the levels. Completeness will love it. The ending clearly hints that another title will follow – certainly with AH as main villain. Spoiler alert: AH will appear in the game and he is bad news.
Level-design: Level design is rather linear with some options to deviate here and there. Later in the game, the hero gets some upgrades, which will emphasize this even more. The game is a Nazi-shooter and one should not expect something from the game is not built around. The attention to detail is exceptional and much more than a shooter ever will need. Locations are diverse. The world of Wolfenstein looks great and feels alive!
Bugs and problems: I first installed the game on my gaming laptop. The game ran ok, but it crashed a few times. Clearly, the system was too weak to handle the title. So, I was disappointed and angry. Then, I installed it on a mid-range PC and the game ran flawless without any problems, at all. On my high-end system, I had not a single issue from start to finish. So, my conclusion is: If you do not run Wolfenstein on a potato, you will have little issues. After future patching and driver updates, issues will be a thing of the past anyways. The game has fewer issues than most AAA titles after launch.
I had one issue with clipping, when I accidently fell through the geometry, but after reloading my save, the problem never repeated.
The only real complaint about the game I have, is that the directional marker is only visible, if you are very close to it. So, often I did not know where to go and had to back-track. This is  very annoying and breaks the experience, as Wolfenstein is all about fluent and continuous action.
Loading times are extremely short. On my RAID0 with two HDDs. Loading a full level takes much less than 10 seconds. This is far below average of most AAA titles.
In conclusion, this is a very good and satisfying game. I call it a true successor and improvement over the previous game. Sure, it is not as a spectacular surprise, as the previous Wolfenstein installment was. This time around people have huge expectations. Still, the sequel builds upon all that made the last game so great. I recommend playing the first game. Without, fresh players will lose a lot of valuable context.
I cannot but advise everyone to not fall for the rage train and complaining in the review section. The game is a stellar example of a faithful and well-made sequel to one of the best shooters ever made.
For a single-player title, it is as good as it gets in 2017. Well done!

I finished this game (story and all filler oberkommando side missions that are not worth doing) and had a great deal of fun, but I find it hard to recommend this game on it's own.
Wolfenstein II tries to be a game that has it's story as one of it's main points of focus. This, in my opinion, is the weakest part of the game that drags everything else down. The moment you start getting into the gameplay and blast nazis while listening to some banging music you get quickly interrupted with some expositional radio chatter or a cutscene.
I feel like this type of approach isn't that acceptable in a game like this and it only disrupts any type of pacing the game might've had.
Without major story spoilers, I can just comment that one of the main reasons I'm addressing this is because the story isn't interesting and the characters behave like idiots way too often (like deploying pregnant women in combat zones on crucial missions) to close your eyes on them and have little to no development or dynamic.
If anything, only high quality voice acting salvages a lot of stupid scenarios you might face up until the credits start to roll (and maybe even beyond in DLC or a sequel, considering some plot points have no resolution).
All of the above would be ok if the game didn't try to portray itself as this serious dramatic story about freedom and revolution (despite having a bunch of jokes here and there) and had a more defined tone.
But as I've said, I had fun: the gameplay is fun when you are allowed to actually play the game. Although, it's not without some problems - the weapon selection is not impressive at all, especially considering that you have two weapons that are waaay stronger than other things you have and level design feels really basic despite having some unusal options for sneaking past enemies or ambushing them.
The reason I'm not recommending this game is simply because Wolfenstein: The New Order has been out for 3 years and it's still a better game that you can get cheaper than Wolfenstein II during it's release week. But if you are finished with The New Order and want some more nazi killing and new content, this game might be a good pick... when it's cheaper.
