The fact this game is still running mostly negative reviews is heartbreaking.
I have 50 hours into this game. I was convinced almost instantly that this game was amazing. I only obtained it recently after alot of patching if I understand correctly. However, patched up; it's now ready to rock. I will make this short and sweet.
- Top 3 Pros -
- Endless -
This game is ridiculously huge. Something that everyone hated on them so bad. This game is simply a pioneer. Sandbox is the best description with the endlessly generated worlds and events. There is always something there, albeit minute or huge.
- Discovery -
Discovering the next class of ship or next planet or next galaxy or next species or.... You get the picture. Granted you can see some repetition but its always different to some level. Even if the species has a tiny set of wings. I mean, I've got to witness flying whales that fed on birds!
- Simplicity -
This appeals to many gamers that do not want some complicated UI or endless customization options to make it comfortable. Smooth transitions into the atmosphere, space combat, experience small level politics, Warping to new universe. Even the story delivery in dialog is short, simple and still captivating.
- Top 3 Cons -
- NPC engagment -
The NPC engagment is there. There is just nothing in depth. A diplomacy meter is used to allow purchasing of Blueprints to progress your character. Which is great. Otherwise, there are limited options.
- ...Simplicity... -
Even the space stations are a little dry. I am okay with reciprocity, makes sense when spreading an empire over the billions of galaxies. However, it's empty. Or repetitive.
- Guide -
The map and large scale navigation for something this HUGE should be direct and easy. It lacks in markings and capability unless using the discoveries box. The story directs you and the main goal of the galaxy directs you. What happens when you begin creating your own map out, making money of mining and needing to note your routes easier.
Summary
I'm not a developer/distributer/pro-gamer. I'm a consumer that has played games as a hobby. I constantly see the trend of when a title drops with alot of hype, everyone throws hate because they launched before a deadline. Alot are justified. This one is a rare case. It's beautiful, intriguing and absolutely mind blowing. A small example of where we stand in our own galaxy. Absolutely wonderful job to everyone that made/making this game possible. I'm excited to see where it goes. Everything has it's drawbacks, but give it a go. Especially while it is on sale.

*THIS REVIEW CONTAINS SPOILERS! YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED*
This is an absolutely fantastic game so far. Everything about it is just perfect.
"Cute terror." Yeah, anything but. This game starts off all cute, it lowers your defenses, and the fear provided up to about room fifty is just cute little jumpscares mixed with a tiny bit of tension.
Upon entering room fifty, *SPOILER* you are met with a pile of green ink and a note. Upon reading said note, you are greeted with the message,
"Spouting, Splashing, Soaking.
Innards, Ingest, Invoking.
Nailing, Never, stops the Choking."
A bit out of place for this cutesy little game isn't it? It caught me off guard and genuinely unsettled me and made me feel unsafe. On top of this,  as soon as you finish reading the note, you begin being chased by a monster, upping the tension just that little bit.
After that, this game just has this gradual, and sort of subtle increase in terror, until this game becomes anything but cute. Each monster, or "Specimen" as they're called here, is even more unsettling than the last. You're greeted with friendly little arcade games some time into the game, but upon playing them, you're greeted with some pretty weird and kind of gruesome♥♥♥♥♥♥ again, showing that this game based on "Cute terror" is more than meets the eye.
*SPOILERS AHEAD*
The Specimen that really managed to intrigue yet terrify me is Specimen #8, AKA the Deer Lord. He's encountered at room five hundred fifty eight I believe, a few rooms after encountering some very unpleasant doe. He begins to make the screen bug out, blur your vision with static, and continues to say phrases like "Join us" or "You slayed my children". If he gets close enough to you, he opens up the black cloak he wears around his body, revealing nothing but a ribcage and a lot of faces. Again, like most things in this game, Specimen #8 took me by surprise and managed to horrify me, right down to his theme, "Your Consenting Mind".
Upon being killed by #8, you're greeted by a loud noise, some flashing images, and this wonderful "And I saw, from eyes that were not mine.
"And I felt, with a fear I could not reason.
They watch us, they invade us.
And keep us happy, committing treason.
To a King we didn't deserve.
To a Son who waits weeping.
That I knew, from knowledge gained while sleeping."
Adorable, isn't it?
Synopsis: Spooky's House of Jumpscares is basically a crescendo. It starts quiet, but gradually gets louder and louder until its climax. This game has yet to include a climax, but from what we have right now, this game is a terrifying experience whose future updates I eagerly await. Download this game right now, it's well worth the wait.

has a lot going for it. Interesting concept, beautiful setting, and an involving story. Unfortunately it also has some potent negative factors.

As a console port, the game handles like a garbage truck sometimes, causing even the simplest movements to become a trying task. Jumping over obstacles is out of the question as invisible walls and even debris blocks Nilin from moving forward. I found myself more often than not getting caught on a droid arm lying on the ground and not being able to get out of its elbow nook. Taking from the popularity of Assassin's Creed, wall climbing and building scaling are the most used method of getting around, but its not FUN! The games sometimes hurtfully linear design means Nilin -must- take one route to her destination, which is a pity during the early game where the slums of future Paris sprawl out in all directions. With all the effort the designers put into building such an amazing area it was a shame to not get to explore it.

Too many cutscenes. Too many too short cutscenes. Too many short in-game cutscenes. There has never been a need for a cutscene in-game every 20ft. It breaks the player out of the story when you take control away from them to walk two steps and then give it back. I could have walked those two steps.

Here is something I really tried to find fun, but was mostly tedious. Build your own combo. Take traits from four different catagories and build a combo that can do huge burst damage, lower cooldown timers, or even heal yourself. Sounds good, right? By the end of the game I had two combo's. A healing combo, and a damage combo that lowered my cooldowns, but it gives you FOUR combo's to build! Each longer and more complicated to remember. If you're the kind of person who can remember which order you placed your kicks and punches in to attain maximum combo awesomeness, then maybe you'll appreciate the combat system a little more than I did. I am apparently dumb and prefer three/five hit combo's to seven/nine hit combo's.
Now what I -DID- like about the combat system was the special abilities. After building enough focus by smashing enemies with your fists you can level the field by using one of Nilin's randomly acquired abilities that you acquired for no reason other than plot and the current enemy demanded it. Not that I wasnt grateful for the cool moves. I had a massive hard-on for the data bomb you could strap to an oppenent in the middle of combat and have him blow up and take out half of the enemies around him. Or the stealth upgrade which came in handy for one shot disabling the guards with shields that zapped you, a-la Arkham stun baton's.
As per usual with almost every game now there was the obligatory "push now for things to happen", but I've come to accept that this is now a thing and it will keep happening. I am indifferent. The boss fights are almost like mid-terms where you take everything you've learned so far and beat someone up who has a name. The final boss culminates -everything- you've learned over the game and makes you use it. Something I personally liked. I'm looking at you TOMB RADIER. Hunt for food and then never hunt for food again.
Now the part of the game that I really liked. I hope to turn you on with this section. I know I haven't sounded like I enjoyed the game, but I did.
You are Nilin: Memory Hunter. You've had your mind wiped and take up arms against the corporation Memorize to not only take back who you are, but to free future Paris from its downward spiral of social media addiction and misery. Armed with nothing but your memory hacking glove and a mysterious guiding figure who refers to himself as "Edge", Nilin must push through a hostile world where she has lived her whole life, but is only seeing for the first time.
Ooooh, sexy right? Yes! I wrote that for -you-. For all its faults, the story and plot are SEXY! It gives you the things a game should give you. A quest of discovery and redemption! Forces trying to stop the discovery and redemption which you then PUNCH IN THE FACE and push onward toward discovery and redemption! What can possibly give the hero an advantage over her enemies?!
This right here? This. Is. The. Bomb. It only happens a few times through the game, which is so sad, BUT, every time it happens you are going to be fully involved in the game. Nilin enters the mind of a character and watches a memory. It is now up to you to rewind the memory and edit small details to acheive a new outcome. This is by far the best part of the game. This is the part of the game that you wait for. Even when done wrong and you have to rewind the memory and start all over again three, four, five times, its still interesting.
I recommend this game for those with controllers. I think it will handle MUCH better than a keyboard/mouse combo.

Ok, full review now, finally finished the game. Hopefully it will be more helpful than beforehand. I really wish the Steam review feature had a "Neutral" or "Leaning" option, because that's really the one thing I need right now writing this, but I digress.
I will start off once again by saying that yes,
TL;DR at bottom.
My specs:
MSI GE62VR Apache Pro
Intel Core i7-6700HQ
NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 3GB DDR5 VRAM
16 GB RAM (DDR4)
I was lucky enough to save up for a pretty decent rig that might last me awhile, but let me tell you: I may have met recommended specs but I still had issues starting up the game.
Obviously, the infamous freezing and crashing (which I still had issues with but were rare), and after starting up a second time I had the fullscreen bug, so as far as first impressions went, I was essentially thinking "welp, Bethesda, you've done it again." Yes, I know they only published the game, but still. I really wish developers would try to make sure their games are as bug-free as possible instead of rushing a game out to meet hype.
For anyone hoping to avoid these issues (though this isnt guaranteed to eliminate the possibility completely), disable Async Compute and change your window setting to "Borderless window" if you play fullscreen like I do 95% of the time. I'm on NVIDIA, and I know some settings are best suited to certain brands, but these have been known to work decently on fixing the problems.
After I did that, I had no problems running the game, but my rig may possibly be the reason why. I was not without issues, however. I did experience random crashes (I think a couple occured when I happened to press both ~ and ESC at the same time by accident).
That being said, however, here's where the real review begins.
I'm fairly easy to impress, not gonna lie, and after getting through issues with PC games I normally forget about them and enjoy the game. That was p much the same here.
:
I've heard people complaining about the story being too short. I'm not THAT great at shooters, and I spent a decent bit of time finishing it (as my playtime attests), but I do kind of agree, it did feel over FAIRLY quickly, but it was well-written and long enough for me to like it. Unfortunately, the cutscenes are what deliver most of the important plot elements 80% of the time, and that goes against the game's favor. The New Order did this as well, but not too many of its cutscenes dragged on as much as this game's did. There's not a WHOLE lot going on that's new here, a gradual revolution against the Nazis that forms after you meet several other characters. As far as story progression goes, I go so far as to say it's essentially just more of The New Order.
Personally, I enjoyed the story, but it won't be for everyone.
Also, thinking about it now, one thing does particularly grate me. The scene in the game where Adolf Hitler appears, while interesting in and of itself, doesn't have a lot going for it. The developers and writers really could have made more of Hitler's appearance as a character, but unfortunately
The characters had a lot of personality going for them, and while they do kind of, as the wise Cr1tikal said in his own review, "stay back at home base, eat, sleep and jack off." I still liked the detail put into them, though wish they could have been in the game with me, maybe bantering to each other and showing more personality and not being restricted to cutscene interaction. Grace and Horton were probably the characters I was most "eh" about, with the former seeming like a cool and badass yet nevertheless stereotypical titular-black-character-in-a-shooter-game type, and the latter basically just being what he was in the E3 trailer, an alcoholic country boy with a thirst for revolution. But aside from all this I did enjoy all the characters' personalities. Not as fleshed-out as the characters from TNO though.
This is basically what was going to be the main event on display, as it seems with any modern game at the moment. The game's visuals are amazingly done thanks to the id Tech 6 engine, which you probably previously at work in DOOM. The volumetric rendering really makes some of the effects look nicer than the usualy 2D sprite tricks I normally see in some games. It tends to have a serious aliasing problem at times, though. Not sure if that's a problem on my end. The facial animations in the cutscenes are remarkable, but suffer in-game. In the latter scenario, they very much have that deer-in-the-headlights uncanny valley-style stare, and the mouth movements are often out of sync with the voice lines and move almost puppet-like, making it a bit unsettling to watch.
The gameplay is fun as hell. Aside from my MANY MANY deaths, there was never a moment where I didn't enjoy the gameplay. The heavy weapons ARE a bit bulky to handle, but were still fun to use once I got used to them, mostly.
The stealth mechanic is probably the element that has taken the biggest hit. It's still there, but the areas where you can use it are very heavily restricted and more often than not very open and don't offer much in the way of hiding spots or ways to sneak up on a guard without being spotted by another. There were times where I felt like the game was pressuring me to take the direct assault path and ♥♥♥♥ the stealth. I never
but I doubt it would have helped things much.
This is the other thing I see people complaining about. I hadn't seen it yet when I saw the complaints, but after finishing the game, I can see what they meant. There's no real drama or tension, or, honestly, even any kind of accomplishment.
the end result felt hollow, like it was missing something. And after you finally do that thing at the end? Instant cutscene and the game ends, clearly ending in a way so as to pave the way for another sequel.
And dear ♥♥♥♥ing Christ, that ending song. Once I knew Twisted Sister's "We're Not Gonna Take It" was playing, I eventually realized that several lines in the ending cutscenes are directly taken from the song. And I really wish I could have laughed at that, but all I did was raise my eyebrow to the heavens and utter a faintly audible
Oh, you think I'm talking about the original song?  No, it's a God-awful metalcore cover by some obscure group which I'm not even sure is an actual band called Veilröth. I LOVE metal, and listen to metalcore at rare times, but Jesus, what were they thinking using this poor excuse of a cover? And it's almost 9 minutes, by the way, spanning the length of the credits, so if you wanna see splash screens and background visuals (it has one splash cutscene), you'll have to sit through it.
In spite of all these issues, however (some glaring ones included), I still very much had a blast with this game, although it could have been more, and replayability is low. If you're still uncertain about buying this after reading this review, do the usual thing and wait for a sale.

Now while looks may be decieving, being only listed as 25 hours, i bought the game of the year edition when it first came out, and wore the disks out, so i bought it on Steam because i did not want to spend the time trying to hunt down new disks, but i degress...
Fallout 3 in of itself, when i started it, ran slow and was difficult for me, it was frustrating at first, but once i got a better computer, and monitor, the difference was amazing! Yes, this was not my old Fallout and Fallout 2, and in one case, i was as glad as ♥♥♥♥ it was not Fallout Tactics. Eventually it grew on me, the story not as much, but the wasteland enviroment, the action, the having to look out for enemies as i least expected it, radiation around every corner, even the random enounters and respawning encounters always had me on my toes. It got to the point where i had to put the difficulty up to very hard everytime to have a good challenge, but i loved it as DC became a death trap of Feral Ghouls, Super Mutants, and Mirelurks. The DLC's were wonderful, some were weaker than the others, I will admit my favorite DLC's between this and New Vegas was in New Vegas, but each had their own unique fun, irregardless if they were good or not.
So to sum it up, for a first attempt, Bethesda really did good. Yes, they could have done better, a lot better. Story needs work, accurate map more based on real life road system would be nice, more variety in weapons, and mods for weapons without using mods, but it was a far better attempt at bring Fallout to a new audience, Better than New Vegas in my humble opinion, but not by much only because of the bugs, and how it can still be more difficult to survive here than in New Vegas. It was a good way to wait as well until i could catch a ride on the Prydwin to the Commonwealth, it was a lot closer to there.
Before i end this, i want to address one more thing, we need to stop this petty infighting in our Fallout community, and come together as one community. Yes, i love all the games, period, end of story, no one game is superior to another, and each game is flawed in their own way. So are humans, if i must remind you all, and if we cannot stop this pointless bickering, one day, we may not have another chance to go back to the wasteland, because our own great war destroyed it.

Endlich ist es soweit! Ein neuer Teil von Deponia aus dem Hause Daedalic ist da! Das Spiel ist ein typisches Point&Click Adventure, wo wir etliche Rätsel lösen mussen. Doch wie lange hab’ ich darauf gewartet? Seitdem 2013 der eigentlich letzte Teil der Serie, Goodbye Deponia, beendet wurde, war es lange Zeit Still um unseren Helden Rufus. Doch nun ist er zurück!
Zeitreisen für Anfänger
Für alle die, den letzten Teil von Deponia nicht gespielt haben sollten, bitte überspringt diesen Absatz. Da man zum Schluss von Chaos auf Deponia quasi den Heldentod stirbt, wobei es nie klar war, ob wir wirklich sterben, kehrt mit Doomsday etwas Neues in die Serie.
In Deponia Doomsday können wir Zeitreisen! Ein spannendes neues Element, womit sich auch glatt ein weiteres Spiel machen lässt. Allerdings ist das nicht die einzige Neuerung, denn gleich zum Tutorial lernen wir das, sag ich mal Klick Event kennen. Dabei musst du so schnell wie möglich die linke Maustaste drücken, um z.B. ene Tür zu zuhalten.
Eine zweite Chance
Der vierte Teil der Serie setzt noch vor den Ereignissen des ersten Spiels ein. Das Erste, was wir erleben ist ein Tutorial mit einem sehr alten Rufus. daraus lässt sich zumindest schließen, dass wir den Sturz im letzten Teil irgendwie überlebt haben. Nach dem Tutirial fängt alles scheinbar mit einem Traum an, aber wer die vorherigen Spiele kennt, weiß dass es die Handlung war, die wir bis dahin kannten. Doch nun wachen wir in einer kleinen Kabine auf und wundern uns über diesen Traum. Wir sind noch mit unserer Freundin Toni zusammen und basteln gerade in einem offensichtlich verstrahlten Gebiet an einem Heißluftballon. Damit wollen wir natürlich Deponia verlassen und nach Elysium fliegen.
Da lernen wir auch schon einen neuen Charakter im Spiel kennen, McChronicle, ein Zeitreisender. Der ist bei weitem nicht der einzige, es kommen ca 70 neue Charaktere auf uns zu in ungefähr 20 Spielstunden.
Scheinbar hat er es geschafft aus einem Auto eine Zeitmaschine zu bauen. Und prompt ist Rufus in die ganze Zeitreise Sache hinein gezogen. Wie wir alle wissen läuft das natürlich nicht ohne Unfälle ab.
Der Tüftler ist wieder da
Auch in Deponia Doomsday gibt es wieder tolle Rätsel. Manchmal zwar recht schwer zu lösen, zumindest war es das für mich und auch recht Sinnfrei zum teil, da man nie auf die Idee kommen würde z.B. eine Klobrille zum Teil einer Falle werden zu lassen.
Aber das macht gerade den Reiz des Spiels aus. Es gibt auch wieder eine menge Witze mit dabei und die Wahl der Synchronsprecher ist auch wieder oberste Schublade! Ich freue mich jedes mal, wenn ich das Spiel starte, dass ich wieder so tolle Stimmen hören kann. So etwas ist doch recht selten, besonders im deutschen Spielemarkt.
Die Steuerung ist auch recht einfach, man braucht quasi nur die Maus und für Tipps gibt es noch die Leertaste. Mit der Leertaste werden alle Objekte angezeigt, die man benutzen kann.

Mein Fazit ist, wer noch keinen Teil von Deponia gespielt hat, sollte das schnell ändern, denn dieser Teil gefällt mir jetzt schon sehr sehr gut. Und wer die anderen Teile schon kennt, für den ist es ein Pflichtkauf! Wer will schon verpassen wie es mit Rufus weitergeht?!

Deponia Doomsday is the fourth installment of Daedelics point-and-click adventure series. It features around 6-10 hours of gameplay and the same high quality art and voice actors (at least the german ones), alongsite the fantastic and wonderous world that is Deponia (if you like tabletop games, check out the Deponia: Roleplaying Game (based on the Fate Trash ruleset)). The puzzles are  mostly logical, that is, point-and-click-adventure-logical. And that is deliberatly so. They are build in a way where you have to ask yourself: "Okay, obviously, this isnt going to be the direct solution. But what kind of methaphors or puns could I use to achive the desired outcome?". If you are looking for logical puzzles, you won't find them here. But then again, if you are playing Deponia Doomsday without having liked the first three, what are you even doing here? There are also some (less fun) mini-games. Thankfully, they are all optional.
There isn't much to say about the technical aspects of the game: It is 2D, so It runs perfectly smooth on my 6 year old notebook.
Once again, it is Deponia, nothing more, nothing less. If you liked the first three games and want to spend some more time with Rufus and friends, do check it out.
In many ways Deponia 3: Goodbye Deponia is the "real ending" of the series. If you were one of those fans who wanted a happy end, spoiler, this isn't going to be one. There can't be a happy end. Why? Because once again you are playing as Rufus. And he is still the same he was in the first game: A sociopath in the real sense of the word, an anti hero per definition with no empathy (or respect) for others. He doesn't think about the cause of his actions, just their effects. And so, yet again, he tries to achieve one simple Goal (ha!), which leads to a downward spiral of chaos. While his actions are motivated by trying to fix previous ones, they too will surely lead to.. but I think we already know that, right? It is Rufus, after all.
There are a lot of in-jokes for the fans, especially those ones who know about the reactions after the second and third part of the series. There are a lot of puns and bad jokes. There is a lot of german humor.
And there is once again Rufus, Goal, Toni and a cast of other characters. If you didn't like the third one, don't play this one. Otherwise, sit back, enjoy the ride and after everything is over, pour yourself a cold one, toast to adventures past and let Rufus have his redemption.
Even if it means to let go.
P.S: It also has one of the funniest (interactive!) building montage scenes in any game I know :D

Hellblade:Senua's Sacrifice is a special kind of beast.
For one, gameplay is lacking. There are long stretches were you just walk around, there's basically one kind of puzzle and combat is, except for one encounter, very repetitive and limited. Also, it is way to short.
These two factors will probably keep the game from becoming the widely recognized classic it deserves to be, which is a shame.
If you manage to immerse yourself in Hellblade, you're in for one of the most intense and unsettling experiences gaming has to offer. The mind of Senua is awash with demons, and Ninja Theory presents them masterfully. The one kind of puzzle in the game? It all revolves around perspective and perception, about finding the right angle to see the world. Combat? Mostly revolves around gaining focus, so Senua can clearly see her enemy instead of stumbling around, trying not to be overwhelmed. And walking around? That's when you get a tour of Senuas mind, guided by the many voices constantly prattling in her head, helpful, comforting, deriding, condescending, accusing.
And here is what I think to be the greatest trick of the game: the voices. They adress not only Senua, but the player as well, creating another persona and thus preventing a strong identification of the player with the character. The player is someone who seems to follow her around, guides her and can also hear her hallucinations. Basically I, who sit in front of the screen, am part of Senuas psychosis, one of the voices. And that, in the words of the Doctor, is absolutely brilliant. I started the game weirded out and a bit annoyed by the voices. About an hour in the game I was feeling tense and uneasy whenever they stopped.
Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice is required playing for everyone who can immerse him/herself in atmosphere and story and who has even a passing interest is psychological horror and/or norse mythology. Stay away if you think story is just something keeping you from your next kill.
Hellblade it's an mind blowing wonderful experience.

While not the first game in this series, this is the one that made it massively popular and, in time, the obnoxious sequel-printer it became. Partly that's because that's just how Activision does things with it's franchises that do well. The other part is that this game is genuinely good, and they've been trying (and failing) to match its quality ever since. There are shooters with better stories, gameplay, and multiplayer, but the combined package you get here is very hard to dismiss. It's all superb quality... well, I can't speak to multiplayer because I barely touched that, but the rest certainly is. It's got the best single-player campaign of the series, with lots of variety in the missions ranging from a night raid on a container ship at sea, massive intense firefights with insane amounts of gunfire, tense sneaky missions where stealth and precision are essential, and an eerie and dehumanizing ride in an AC-130 gunship where you blow away dozens of hostiles from thousands of feet in the air who can't do anything back to you. It's all excellent gameplay, and the story you get with it is, while not totally spectacular, much better than average for first person shooters.
Even if you find this series at present irritating and bland (I do), this game at least is still worth checking out. After having played it, it's not hard to understand why its immediate sequels were breaking sales records.

Despite the bad start, this game has taken shape, just watch the videos the devs have put up.   I have only spent 6 hours playing this game and found I could not put it down.  You start off in the main game trying to repair your damaged crashed space ship.   You have to find all the elements to get it off into space.  What was fun for me was trying to find all the elements, accidently using some zinc to upgrade some of my equipment and that forcing me to find more.  I also used this other element I needed to fix my engines.  The upgrades are a must and help a great deal.  The other fun part was I was on a hot planet and my suit would only keep a shield so long, so I had to either run back to get into my ship to refresh it, or find elements on the planet that I could use to recharge it.  This can be a challenging game, but super fun, and when you take off from the planet you feel satisfied at repairing your ship.  What is really cool is taking off from the planet and seeing space come into view and watching the planet get smaller as you fly away.  I docked with an alien freighter who wanted to sell me his ship for more units that I had, which was 0.  For those that say this is a relaxing game, I can see the point, but there is some excitement the devs have added, there are attack drones, and also some of the plants will attack you as well.  There will be space combat, but I have not run into it as I just got space worthy.  I would get this game in a sale, just because I am cheap.

The fact this game is still running mostly negative reviews is heartbreaking.
I have 50 hours into this game. I was convinced almost instantly that this game was amazing. I only obtained it recently after alot of patching if I understand correctly. However, patched up; it's now ready to rock. I will make this short and sweet.
- Top 3 Pros -
- Endless -
This game is ridiculously huge. Something that everyone hated on them so bad. This game is simply a pioneer. Sandbox is the best description with the endlessly generated worlds and events. There is always something there, albeit minute or huge.
- Discovery -
Discovering the next class of ship or next planet or next galaxy or next species or.... You get the picture. Granted you can see some repetition but its always different to some level. Even if the species has a tiny set of wings. I mean, I've got to witness flying whales that fed on birds!
- Simplicity -
This appeals to many gamers that do not want some complicated UI or endless customization options to make it comfortable. Smooth transitions into the atmosphere, space combat, experience small level politics, Warping to new universe. Even the story delivery in dialog is short, simple and still captivating.
- Top 3 Cons -
- NPC engagment -
The NPC engagment is there. There is just nothing in depth. A diplomacy meter is used to allow purchasing of Blueprints to progress your character. Which is great. Otherwise, there are limited options.
- ...Simplicity... -
Even the space stations are a little dry. I am okay with reciprocity, makes sense when spreading an empire over the billions of galaxies. However, it's empty. Or repetitive.
- Guide -
The map and large scale navigation for something this HUGE should be direct and easy. It lacks in markings and capability unless using the discoveries box. The story directs you and the main goal of the galaxy directs you. What happens when you begin creating your own map out, making money of mining and needing to note your routes easier.
Summary
I'm not a developer/distributer/pro-gamer. I'm a consumer that has played games as a hobby. I constantly see the trend of when a title drops with alot of hype, everyone throws hate because they launched before a deadline. Alot are justified. This one is a rare case. It's beautiful, intriguing and absolutely mind blowing. A small example of where we stand in our own galaxy. Absolutely wonderful job to everyone that made/making this game possible. Remember Me
At first, I was very wary of this action-adventure game set in a cyberpunk setting. It had mixed reviews and while the game is far from perfection, I can't say Remembe Me is bad. Far from it actually! But sadly, there is a few irritants that unable Remember Me to be outstanding. To make it short, you are Nilin, a memory hunter, in Neo-Paris set in 2084, that somehow, got herself arrested and get's a mindwipe that erases most of your memories. You're liberated from a shady contact, called Edge, who wants you to remember who you really are and also, wants to change  the world as they know it since it is very repressed. The people in this game's world buy/sell memories either good/bad like some simple commodity. There is some addicts who are living in the slums and they've lost mostly if not all their personality.
The gameplay is quite similar to the Batman Arkham games except don't expect a "detective mode" when you're roaming the places. The combat is almost a direct copy of Arkham's except you setup your own combos how you want them once you have unlocked sufficient points. It took me a while to figure out how it works but once you do understand it, the gameplay will be much easier! I played the whole game with the Xbox 360 gamepad since the Keyboard and Mouse controls were really atrocious in this game. But the controls, even on the XB360 gamepad, they're very wonky and even laggish... and during combat, you can't have wonky unresponsive controls!
The story unfolds at a good pace. Total playtime is fairly decent for a modern game as they usually clock under 10 hours. The platforming moments are pretty easy as they're highlighted properly. Remember Me has a few Quick-Time Events that mostly occurs on bosses and they aren't too intrusive. There's a few puzzles mostly towards the last three episodes and they're fairly easy to resolve!
My gripes are mainly on the movements. Secondly would be the annoying patrolling drones that you can't disable, only evade they're detection field.
PROS:
+Fascinating dark vision of the future.
+Truly impressive visuals (graphics, 3D modeling, etc).
+Fitting soundtrack on this cyberpunk world.
+Remixing memories (manipulating memories) is a cool feature enabling you to craft memories into an individual.
+Edward Snowden would love this game... as it explores hot-topic issues like surveillance and social media.
+Nilin is a strong protagonist that make's her feelsvery human.
CONS:
-Cumbersome camera that get's in the way very often.
-Ordinary and stiff combat that get's frustrating at times, until you figure out how the combo-setup/system works.
-Extremely linear and little exploration. Level design feels constricting. You see the superb Paris on backgrounds yet you never get to explore much.
-Not enough Memory Remix and sadly, only to main characters. Would have been greater to do that at others!
-Dialogue is mostly all cheesy in this game.
-British accents for French citizens? Hmm... something's wrong here!
-Little replay value (only if you seek all achievements and collectibles that is!).
OVERALL:
A fun game that has a few irritants which holds Remember Me from being a very good game. Granted it is DONTNOD Entertainment's first game and clearly, these irritants can easily be fixed in a possible sequel or another similar game. The combat and platforming are the least interesting parts of Remember Me, and they're what you'll be doing most. You don't have much exploration to do as once you reach a certain area, you're locked out. Though Neo-Paris is unforgettable, your journey through it isn't.
RECOMMENDATION:
Yes, I do recommend this game. If you can ignore its issues, you're surely going to enjoy Remember Me. It's not a perfect action-adventure game but in my opinion, it get's the job done in entertainement!
RATING:
7.0 / 10

The Matrix meets Inception, that is perhaps giving it a little too much credit. Set in a cyberpunk future "Neo-Paris" where memories can be copied, shared or stolen. Remember Me has style for sure however when it comes to one of the most central parts of the game: the combat, it falls short.
I wouldn't recommend playing with mouse and keyboard if you have a controller, I played with an xbox controller and even that felt clunky. The combat is frustrating for a number of reasons, there is no Lock-on feature when fighting, the only lock on is for your ranged weapon.
Dodging is awkward and a little buggy sometimes you can find yourself stuck in a dogpile of enemies if you do not compensate for that eventualilty.
The combos can be really hard to pull off even though they aren't that complex buttonwise, the problem is when fighting multiple enemies one always sneaks in a jab and breaks your combo, you can dodge and resume the combo but the time you're given to do so is very short.
The combo editing system had the potential to be really awesome mixing and matching damage, health regen, cooldown reset and multiplier moves however it simply isn't mainly because a jack of all trades combo set isn't good at anything and you are much better off focusing one of the four sets soley to do damage or regen health ect.
7/10. Great visuals and story, great sound design and voice acting, poor music however and then of course the flawed combat.

Ok, full review now, finally finished the game. Hopefully it will be more helpful than beforehand. I really wish the Steam review feature had a "Neutral" or "Leaning" option, because that's really the one thing I need right now writing this, but I digress.
I will start off once again by saying that yes,
TL;DR at bottom.
My specs:
MSI GE62VR Apache Pro
Intel Core i7-6700HQ
NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 3GB DDR5 VRAM

I was lucky enough to save up for a pretty decent rig that might last me awhile, but let me tell you: I may have met recommended specs but I still had issues starting up the game.
Obviously, the infamous freezing and crashing (which I still had issues with but were rare), and after starting up a second time I had the fullscreen bug, so as far as first impressions went, I was essentially thinking "welp, Bethesda, you've done it again." Yes, I know they only published the game, but still. I really wish developers would try to make sure their games are as bug-free as possible instead of rushing a game out to meet hype.
For anyone hoping to avoid these issues (though this isnt guaranteed to eliminate the possibility completely), disable Async Compute and change your window setting to "Borderless window" if you play fullscreen like I do 95% of the time. I'm on NVIDIA, and I know some settings are best suited to certain brands, but these have been known to work decently on fixing the problems.
After I did that, I had no problems running the game, but my rig may possibly be the reason why. I was not without issues, however. I did experience random crashes (I think a couple occured when I happened to press both ~ and ESC at the same time by accident).
That being said, however, here's where the real review begins.
I'm fairly easy to impress, not gonna lie, and after getting through issues with PC games I normally forget about them and enjoy the game. That was p much the same here.
:
I've heard people complaining about the story being too short. I'm not THAT great at shooters, and I spent a decent bit of time finishing it (as my playtime attests), but I do kind of agree, it did feel over FAIRLY quickly, but it was well-written and long enough for me to like it. Unfortunately, the cutscenes are what deliver most of the important plot elements 80% of the time, and that goes against the game's favor. The New Order did this as well, but not too many of its cutscenes dragged on as much as this game's did. There's not a WHOLE lot going on that's new here, a gradual revolution against the Nazis that forms after you meet several other characters. As far as story progression goes, I go so far as to say it's essentially just more of The New Order.
Personally, I enjoyed the story, but it won't be for everyone.
Also, thinking about it now, one thing does particularly grate me. The scene in the game where Adolf Hitler appears, while interesting in and of itself, doesn't have a lot going for it. The developers and writers really could have made more of Hitler's appearance as a character, but unfortunately
The characters had a lot of personality going for them, and while they do kind of, as the wise Cr1tikal said in his own review, "stay back at home base, eat, sleep and jack off." I still liked the detail put into them, though wish they could have been in the game with me, maybe bantering to each other and showing more personality and not being restricted to cutscene interaction. Grace and Horton were probably the characters I was most "eh" about, with the former seeming like a cool and badass yet nevertheless stereotypical titular-black-character-in-a-shooter-game type, and the latter basically just being what he was in the E3 trailer, an alcoholic country boy with a thirst for revolution. But aside from all this I did enjoy all the characters' personalities. Not as fleshed-out as the characters from TNO though.
This is basically what was going to be the main event on display, as it seems with any modern game at the moment. The game's visuals are amazingly done thanks to the id Tech 6 engine, which you probably previously at work in DOOM. The volumetric rendering really makes some of the effects look nicer than the usualy 2D sprite tricks I normally see in some games. It tends to have a serious aliasing problem at times, though. Not sure if that's a problem on my end. The facial animations in the cutscenes are remarkable, but suffer in-game. In the latter scenario, they very much have that deer-in-the-headlights uncanny valley-style stare, and the mouth movements are often out of sync with the voice lines and move almost puppet-like, making it a bit unsettling to watch.
The gameplay is fun as hell. Aside from my MANY MANY deaths, there was never a moment where I didn't enjoy the gameplay. The heavy weapons ARE a bit bulky to handle, but were still fun to use once I got used to them, mostly.
The stealth mechanic is probably the element that has taken the biggest hit. It's still there, but the areas where you can use it are very heavily restricted and more often than not very open and don't offer much in the way of hiding spots or ways to sneak up on a guard without being spotted by another. Some people bashed this for not being "the old Fallout", but I think it sits well between the feel of the original two games (excluding the series spinoffs) and Bethesda's strength of making first-person RPGs. And the GOTY version is the best version, obviously.
Graphically, its quite dated, but that can be fixed somewhat with mods and such, and the green filter doesn't help (again, fixable with mods), but there's something amazing about playing this game after being away from it that keeps me coming back. While it uses a slightly-modified rendition of the same version of the Gamebryo engine that
was run on, the potato-faced people are gone, but the zoom-in-to-speak-to-people aspect remains, making some conversations feel a bit...
personal. Regardless, if you can overlook the quirks of the game's visuals (and its occasional hiccup), the graphics don't hamper the game too much.
Gameplay-wise, Bethesda attempted to blend FPS combat with some of the %age-based gameplay from yesteryear in the form of the VATS system. Sometimes it works to use FPS, other times VATS is the way to go; its up to you to decide which you like to use. Although, in the late-game, you become a demigod and hit practically anything you aim at in VATS, so I find myself getting used to that more often than not. Also, the lockpick mechanic is a synch compared to other games, so once your score is high enough you can unlock anything that doesn't require a key to open. WHich is most of the open-abled doors/drawers/boxes in the game.
The story is possibly the weak spot; it's your generic "save the world" dealie, but for the most part it works. But looking back after having played
, this entry feels somewhat... lacking. Certainly not to the degree of
, but there is definitely an arrow missing from its quiver that makes the game feel a little less interesting. Still, the world at large is engaging enough to engross you for hours on end, if you can get around the feeling that you're leaving your main quest in what I like ot call "RPG Quest Limbo".
Lastly, I should probably talk about mods, because while FO3 is fun on its own, it was never the most stable or best-looking game, even at the time. Look around ModDB or the Fallout Nexus (just Google those and you'll find the sights) for visual and runtime enhancements for your first venture into the Capitol Wasteland, unless you don't mind floundering when the game bugs the hell out, or if you only plan on playing the game for a few hours then quitting for a long time. It is worth the time, and installing mods is not too difficult, as long as you understand how to install & run them. Getting the FoMM (Fallout Mod Manager) is generally necessary for starting the game with mods (you don't need to start it from Steam either!), but again, it's not hard to wrap one's brain around.
After you've gotten used to the basic mods, there's a plethora of others to add in. Just be aware that not all mods will be compatible with each other. Check to make sure that they are usable with one another, or it could REALLY screw up your game.
Overall,
is a hell of an experience, and worth a run-through of the first couple of hours at least, if just for the feeling of awe that one feels upon entering the Wasteland for the first time.

The story isn’t as focused as it could’ve been and spends most of its time justifying the trilogy’s ending in some moments that feel more like lecturing than fun. Trine is a platformer with an ok story, good atmosphere and beautiful level art and very tight controls.
+ Good atmosphere coming from good music and beautiful level art
+ Ok story
+ Upgradeable characters
+ Almost always tight controls
+ Repeating levels isn't dull
0 Ok enemy AI
- Not all characters fully upgradeable
- Not too great enemy variety
- Pretty short game
- When in level there is no way to see its name
After the prologue the player switches between and controls one of three characters - you can think of them as three skill load-outs, thief, wizard and knight - to fight not a great variety of enemies and solve puzzles. Puzzles aren't hard but not too easy.
The story is ok but didn't really get me interested. Some of it is told while levels load and only accompanied by a rather simple map tracking progress, some of it is narrated in-game and there is a bit of character development when the three characters speak up on occasion. It seems to me like not a lot of time was put into the story and story art.
The game gets a bit harder by introducing harder versions of the standard enemy, from time to time a new enemy, and mostly and most interestingly new perils; and easier by gradually upgrading the three characters and outfitting them with artefacts.
The AI of enemies is not great. Enemies can platform to you, correctly estimate distance for ranged attacks but also kill themselves, e.g. jump into spike pits, and inadvertently kill each other.
Collecting experience pieces more or less hidden throughout the level and gained by killing enemies gives upgrade points at constant intervals. There is no grinding as such, each level has a set amount of experience to collect. You may need to play levels multiple times to find all the experience - good thing the most heart has been put into level designs and they aren't dull at all.
Upgrade points are distributed per characters, so each point can be used sort of three times. I dislike that not all characters are fully upgradeable.
Along with experience pieces you sometimes find chests containing artefacts that can be distributed between characters to varying impact.
The controls are very tight. The only irritating thing I found was the grab ability of the wizard depends on material type and at some points the composition of things unnecessarily changes making me "grab"  multiple times and disrupting flow.
One minor irritating thing I encounter in games is the impossibility of determining where I am. Certain achievements are bound to specific levels yet when inside one I don't know how to figure out which one it is. You can select the level by name from the main menu and its name is inconspicuously displayed at load time. In-level there is no appropriate display.
The game appears to be quite short. Completing everything will get you some adequate game time though.
I liked Trine and am looking forward to playing the apparently even more beautiful Trine 2. Recommended.

I just finished Trine to 100% completion.
The game is really fun to play most of the time; and well worth the investment if you're looking to kill time in a beautifully themed puzzle platformer with a couple of friends.
It relishes in its simplicity. It's pretty. The music is great. You can play with two other friends, all with unique characters and playstyles. The puzzles can be solved with relative ease due to the varied toolkit the protagonists offer. Its got a lighthearted air of humor about it that makes it legitimately enjoyable.
That being said, it's not particularly revolutionary. The puzzles aren't challenging. The combat is a little redundant and, in most cases, feels unnecessary. 90% of the challenge seems to come from wrestling the physics system and getting knocked about in all sorts of ways.
If you're looking for anything more than a few hours of silliness, I would look elsewhere--and no matter what, I would recommend waiting until it goes on sale before buying. $15 feels a little steep given its age and the experience itself.

I don't often write reviews but I feel like it is necessary to write one for this game.
Ori and the Blind Forest is such a great game. The art style is so beautiful, the soundtrack absolutely amazing, and the story the game is telling very sweet and lovely.
It can be quite frustrating at some points (I ragequit the game very early on and didn't wanna play it for a week; only to then complete the rest of the game in one sitting), but it definitely gets easier the more you play - even though the game itself gets harder the further you progress. Usually I'm not a huge fan of platformers, but this game had me hooked instantly - for the above mentioned reasons.
You get to spend your skill points just as you like, and you can explore and revisit areas - despite mission goals - completely freely most of the time (with the exceptions of three areas that you can't revisit) once you learn the required moves to access them.
The controls are very easy and not complicated at all, though you can't remap them if you wanted to.
Also, some of the achievements are kinda bugged; it's not that you cannot get them though, it's that it's possible that they unlock at completely random times. For example, I randomly got six achievements at once at some point when I only should have gotten one.
Even though I got quite mad at it at one point, I absolutely recommend the game because of its gorgeous art and story.

Personally, I have not run into any technical issues whatsoever. I have a GTX 970 (MSI) and a i5-4690k and get 60-90 fps on Mein Leben (max settings). From what I have experienced, it is very well optimized. I see that many others ARE having issues with the game, so once some of those things are fixed, you can expect this game to run superbly.
As for the game, here are some pros and cons.
Pros:
- Diverse/interesting cast of characters
- Realistic and unfiltered potrayal of what we would expect from the time and setting
- Great gunplay
- Very detailed environments
- Quite challenging on the hardest difficulty available from the start
- Game runs smoothly
- Mechanics work great
- I can shoot and be shot through tiny cracks in plated railings, etc. (realism/attention to detail)
- You get to kill Nazis
Cons (nit-picking for me):
- Some people having technical issues
- If you are on an easy difficulty the game can feel kinda short
- Could have gone way more in-depth with the story and made it more interesting
- Game could have looked quite a bit better
- Not enough weapons or unlocks in the later half of the game to keep things interesting
Overall, there are some thngs that will detract from the games value for some people, but the cons have not been a big deal for me at all, and I have been enjoying this game just fine and would totally recommend getting it.

Call of Duty 4 Modern Warfare is a  first-person shooter action video game developed by Infinity Ward and published by Activision 2007 .
Groups of Marines and British SAS must fight an ultranationalist group that plans a third world war . The player plays as various characters in the story. Yet the narrative is linear and the game looking to get a cinematic effect .
COD 4 Modern Warfare renewed the graphics engine of the previous games in the series in a big way. It had great success and to some extent became the spiritual successor of Counter Strike . It had two sequels that continue the story to its end in Modern Warfare 3. The game has a very mature multiplayer component where the player can call air attacks and reconnaissance vehicles.
Call of Duty 4 Modern Warfare really innovated in the genre. It took the war to the modern era , a battle without pause and film like scenes. Hundreds of shots , stealth, sniper attacks , and a variety of weapons immerse us in this world war. In fact , although the following Call of Duty are much more up to date, they seem an extension of this brilliant game . The feeling of being in the ghost town near  Pipriat Chernobyl is shocking , COD MW4 was technologically wonderful in 2007.
The game sold over 13 million copies in two years and obtained a score of 94 out of 100 on sites like Metacritic or GameRankings .
The game was released for Windows PC , PS3 and XBOX 360. The windows version required  DirectX 9.0c API  . While it requires a graphics card, the game has very low requirements for the graphic quality it has.

Taking place in 2011, Call of Duty 4 introduces us to Khaled Al-Asad, a military learder in a small unnamed Middle Eastern country who stages a coup d'etat siezing control over  the country's government. Meanwhile, a tanker carrying Nukes sinks despite the efforts of British SAS forces to locate and secure them. The story is little more than a xenophobic Neo-con's wet dream.  Given the fact that it takes some inspiration from real world events it's a shame that the geo-political history and culture of the area is not touched on. Instead Modern Warfare paints it's antagonists as angry faced, power hungry anti-westerners with nothing but contempt and hatred for capitalism and democracy while it's protagonists are hardened military super heroes on the side of justice and nobility. This narrative is constructed by briefings between missions that lead into the events at hand. Small story scenes occasional occur during missions to add to the events but the narrative mostly takes a back seat to mission set pieces. As a result pacing is nonexistant—Modern Warfare is a five hour sprint from where the story starts to it's silly, rushed conclusion.
The gunplay is commendable with a large collection of weapons intuitive controls.  While the mechanics are solid missions are undermined by an over reliance on scripting. After a few missions it becomes apparent that you are playing the most sophisticated version of whack a mole ever devised. Enemies flood the battlefield in a seemingly endless stream while you push back until reaching a checkpoint. This design drastically reduces replayability as well as making the systems at play painfully apparent. All games employ smoke and mirrors to cover up the programed logic that makes up their worlds. The best games have you thinking less about whats going on behind the scenes while the worst ones might as well be an open text file with their code on your screen. Modern Warfare's commitment to scripts results in a tightly controlled game play affair that is easily exploitable and ultimately unfulfilling as a result of the semi transparent gameplay curtain draped over it's underpinings.
The real draw for Call of Duty 4 is it's oft imitated multiplayer. Deathmatch, capture the point and free for all variants are all present and accounted for. Where Call of Duty is emulated is through it's ranking system. As you level you earn new weapons, attachments and perks. Challenges are also available that provide bonus experience upon completion. This system does a tremendous job of dangling a carrot in front of it's players. The only other unique feature in Call of Duty's multiplayer feature set are kill streaks, these bonuses are designed to reward skilled play by giving players access to additional tools by racking up kills without dying. UAVs, airstrikes, attack choppers and recon are all at your disposal if you managed to frag enough people without eating a hollow point sandwich yourself. The problem with this system is that it makes balanced match ups much more difficult to find. Two players that are doing well on a single team can deploy killstreak rewards that shift the match in their favor despite the other team being consistently more skilled. It doesn't make sense to further reward people that are already dominant.
Call of Duty 4's accessibility, break neck pace and rewarding multiplayer rank system have given it a tremendous appeal to both hardcore and more casual gamers. The rewards and incentives of multiplayer's ranking system divert attention from it's otherwise standard fare offerings. It's million thrills a second single player experience pushes the average player's attention away from it's reliance on scripting and by relegating it's narrative to briefings and short cutscenes during missions insures that it's lack of depth is inconsequential.  In the end one of the most successful shooters of the past decade is more about spectacle than substance.

I had heard about this game on several gaming websites and on reviews here on Steam. I decided to give it a try and I have to say it was well-worth 29.99 Euro I have spent in a while. The setting intrigued me from the start, even more so Senua's backstory and her ongoing battle with psychosis.
I've played a lot of games but this was the first game that I have played that included such detailed representation of psychosis and the issues that come with it. Even more frightening to think that for centuries, if not millenia, thousands if not millions had to endure such problems, not knowing what is affecting them and having to carry on with life.
Gameplay-wise, it is simplistic. Many might find fault with this but for me it worked beautifully as this is a story-driven game, not a gameplay one. The fighting works in the context of the story, battling out monsters and beasts straight from Norse mythology.  It's not a 'God of War' style game, where you end up fighting an entire pantheon of gods, just those relevant to the story.
Every aspect of this game compliments each other; from the visuals to the story to the music. Oh the music! Ninja Theory, you really need to release this soundtrack! The voice acting is top notch, even more surprising considering the actress that played Senua had no acting experience before!
Overall, for those people who want a story-driven game, I say go for it! Those that want gameplay, I still say get it. The theme of the game is so different and groundbreaking, it would be worth it!

In a moment in gaming history where most games aim for mindless replayability with zero meaning other than "to kill time" and online-only features (sometimes even in single player!"), filled with worthless microtransactions and whatnot, comes Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice to remind everyone that games can be more than just a fun time and deliver an amazing experience with a message, and this game's message rivals (even surpasses) many other big installments'.
The way the game delivers the story is very enjoyable. It's not a story that right away reveals the motivations and backstory of the character. This is a "self-discovery journey" for Senua AND the player, which makes connecting with her easy without feeling like it was forced. You WILL suffer, cry, be desperate, scared, hopeless, but also enjoy with her the moments of melancholy, determination and beauty, thanks to the amazing acting done by Melina Juergens as Senua both in VO and Mo Cap performance (she has my vote as best female performer for this year's many game awards guaranteed).
Definitely a must-play with headphones, since the effect of the binaural dialogues will become greater and will "drive you crazy" as intended by Senua's psychosis. That and the amazing work by the audio department + the amazing soundtrack are more enjoyable with headphones on.
But let's not ignore the work done by the rest of Ninja Theory's team. The artistic direction and level design are really good too. The writing is superb, and the fact that the team didn't take the cheap route and said "yah, she sees things and stuff because she's schizophrenic" but did actual research on the subject and respectfully portrayed it in the game is what makes this experience so delightful. You don't question or think about how weird everything that's happening around Senua is. You just accept this is her version of reality.
But all praise done, let's be fair: this was conceived as a "mid-sized game", and it certainly is. Re-playability is low and the combat mechanics, while entertaing, can feel a little simplistic at first. It does get better as you progress, but not by a great amount (Boss Fights are on a very different league though). Still, I would love a "horde mode" to be implemented. Another thing I see a lot of people complain about is that there is a lot of "walking simulation" in this, and that is also correct, but from my point of view, having this game be all "action packed combat" would not only make it monotonous, it would defeat the sense of progress in the journey Senua takes by removing the quiet and peacefully moments during this "walking simulation" parts that heavily contrast the harsh moments she goes through. You would not believe she's emotionally suffering if all you see is a girl hack n' slashing all the time. Still, if you're not into "walking simulators" this game will probably bore you. You must come to this game for the whole experience itself, not just the gameplay and/or the looks.
This is a game that has become one of my all time favorites.
"The hardest battles are fought in the mind" <- A quote from the game. This applies not only to Senua, but to all of us. By the end of the game, you will realize that there is nothing wrong with the way Senua sees things.
PS: By all means, check the Hellblade Feature included in the game after finishing it. Beautifully done.

One of the best games of the franchise, the highly acclaimed Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare is a must have for a fan of the Call of Duty games. The games single player experience is phenomonal. From the beginning raid on the Russian tanker, to the cataclysmic end to the U.S campaign, to the brilliant All Ghillied Up mission, the game will keep you hooked, followed by a story that is believable, but not over the top compared to the future releases in the franchise.
The Multiplayer is where Call of Duty shines however, and Cod 4 is a thoroughly enjoyable experience but not without flaws due to a variety of reasons at this point in time. When Cod 4 was released, the game included many new features not seen in previous Call of Duty games, such as the now standard Create a Class, Killstreaks etc, all of which feel balanced and nothing too overpowered (except maybe the P90). Where the PC version differs to the console versions is the player count. Cod 4 supports up to 48 players per server and sometimes it's absolute madness, just like the old Call of Duty days. Make no mistake, it's still a really enjoyable experience but console players may find it somewhat jarring coming from console to PC but you can always join a server with less players. There is no Prestige, with ranks taking longer to achieve in its place, and dedicated servers are there which mean less lag compared to the console version.
BUT unfortunately, as 2013, Cod 4's server browser and online experience is somewhat annoying. A LOT of servers which turn up in the browser have this annoying redirect mod, which you have to install. This means what may show up as Backlot, standard, TDM, 40 players may redirect you to a Hardcore, S&D, 3 player game. It's frustrating at times to find a decent game.
All in all, the game is highly recommended and along with the original Cod, UO and Cod 2. Probably the last GREAT Cod, with future games removing much of the standard PC features and instead being a console port. Buy it.

When the game was in Early Access, it was getting boring quickly. You just travelled around the world unlocking things.
But the full version feels like a completely different game.
Instead of giving the player all the tools to build things, they are given one by one, and each tool has a video tutorial.
Instead of just running past characters, killing them or saying hi, you have to complete unique quests: bring an item, take a photo of something, kill someone, build a house, save somebody... This is way better.
Now instead of being in one endless world, you have to travel through endless amount of small worlds, which makes this game less of a minecraft clone.
The chests now contain not only items, but also blueprints and gold bricks...
Gold bricks. They can be obtained by completing quests or found in chests. And you need them to progress through story...
Story. This game finally has a story. This game finally has a goal to achieve.
Just... This is not the Lego Worlds I remember. This is WAAAY better.
I waited for this for 2 years. It was worth it.
(Also, the full game costs 6 times more money than early access, but it is worth the money!)
(Also, if your game runs at 1-3 FPS, change to DirectX 9 in settings, and then restart the game, it should fix it)

In contrast to the previous titles, Deponia 4's puzzles are more straightforward. And the mini-games are a little easier. But there is only one song sung. And overall there is very few new music. But the artwork is good as always.

The issue cannot be avoided; the question of whether many of you will purchase this game will hinge on whether it changes an ending you dislike.  It is important, I think, for you to know it
before you buy; that much is only fair.  However, as a former member of the "I hate that stupid ending!" camp, I strongly urge you to give
a play, as you will otherwise not only miss one of the best adventure games of this decade, but will forego a massive amount of story and character development that puts certain things in context -- and gives a whole new perspective on the shocking end of Rufus' saga as seen in
.
is unquestionably the best Deponia game and most likely the best point-and-click in Daedelic's estimable library.  Its puzzles are brilliant, walking the line between between transparent fairness and lunatic absurdity with unwavering perfection.  It has a more spot-on translation than any Daedelic game to date, and considering how well-done many of their games are in that regard -- particularly the other Deponias -- that says a lot.  As any veteran Elysian geneticist will assure you, it has the funniest gags in the whole series.  It has more varied environments, more lavish animations and even more minigames than any previous Deponia or Daedalic game.  I encountered no bugs, and this is surprising as even the best adventures (like all games) tend to have their share.  What is most important, it has a terrific story, one so wonderfully, maniacally convoluted that it could be mistaken for a cracked Metal Gear Solid -- and looking beyond Poki's impressive feats of Kojima-esque plot engineering, it provides something truly vital for hardcore Deponia fans:  a meatier build-up to, and greater rationale for, Rufus' ultimate decision in
.  It completely changed how I felt about the end of the previous game, and I consider that no small accomplishment.
is a stroke of genius; it's as good as the genre gets.  I know that I will never get any new Rufus adventures, but I look forward to playing back through the series someday with the renewed appreciation that this amazing installment has granted me.  Perhaps if we are lucky (and we stop bombarding Poki with our demands and thus burning him out on the whole thing), we will get to experience the world of Deponia through the eyes of some other character in the future, like Goal or maybe even Bozo.  One can only hope!

An extremely fun game to play with friends and randoms alike, due to the concept of being hunted by sharks. Picked this up during the free weekend + sale with no regrets, after seeing that reviews were better than I expected.
The reason it's okay with randoms is that it's such a fast and different experience to anything else out there so far, and there's something about being able to drop into the ocean and fight off hyper-intelligent sharks.
The game is pretty old, so I don't expect the game to change much by now.
I want to start off saying that this isn't a game that is going to blow your mind, but it's more of a pleasant tickle of sorts. This is
an underwater sim. It's a fast paced underwater asymmetrical action-excursion that takes place in short matches (in the Blood and Gold gamemode, of 2 sharks and 4 divers), so be forewarned.
It's a very original shooter, and its easily most popular and well-thought-out game mode Blood and Gold, takes a couple cues from MOBA style games. To put it very briefly, there's a concept of early, mid, and late game in this mode and different builds suited for different sharks and situations. Even some "gold management" for the divers. It's very unusual but surprisingly interesting. I won't go into detail about this, but I'd suggest looking up some guides or articles that describe the game flow in Depth (pun unintended).
In Depth, sharks and divers really do feel like they're underwater and everything moves very fluidly. Aside from having trouble picking up treasure on occasion (which really isn't even that big of a problem), everything feels really solid. The sharks are unique and each have specialties and baseline stats that are suited for different playstyles. Divers are given a number of character models to choose from, and a both suitable and fun arsenal to customize how they want to play, each match.
Similar to that of Spies vs Mercs from the Splinter Cell series, Depth's contrast between playing sharks versus the divers is an extremely strong one, and really helps further make the game interesting. Sharks are given a well done third person view over their shark, while divers are given the traditional first person camera view. Because they have set up the camera this way, playing as a diver can feel very daunting when knowing that a shark could sweep in and chew you  up. As a shark, you feel empowered and dangerous, but also often vulnerable against the power of human technology if you're not careful enough.
There's a sense of play with shadows and the fogginess of the deep that is really well done, and plays to the game's advantage. As a diver, you are given an ample arsenal to work with in fending off the sharks as you traverse your brief underwater excursion, but there's nothing that'll shake the feeling that comes with knowing a shark could appear at any time just outside of your view. The devs have done a great job in making it look and feel really authentic, even if this isn't a likely scenario. The underwater sounds are also pretty great, and do the job at conveying the setting well, while playing a role as a gameplay mechanic, too.
The only thing that I would ask for at this point in time is just more maps, really (although any meaty content would be great regardless). There's already plenty to dig into, but more is always better in a game like this. There is definitely a learning curve to the game, and lots to learn if you want to be an expert at Depth.
New modes wouldn't hurt either, but the game's been out for a while already.
Most asymmetrical team games become very dull and pretty uninteresting after a few plays, but I think this is one that my friends and I can come back to from time to time and really enjoy together. It's definitely something else, and your mileage with the game can vary depending on what you're looking for from Depth.

This game combines the two controls, forcing you to always look towards the horizon. Can't look up or down. Darkness is your friend because the map will only show your position when this lighting condition is active. In the light, it disappears! It's been almost two years since I played the sequel (Trine 2) to this game (Trine). Characters are different, Wizard can create object and manipulate them, Thief can use arrows to kill enemy's, fire arrows to light torches and she also has grappling arrows. Knight is made mostly for fighting, but he can use shield to throw objects and his mace to break things. I enjoyed how fast this game is for puzzler but at the same time that might be a problem for some people (because sometimes you will need to act really fast and someone might want nice and easy puzzles). Game looks good, backgrounds are ok, story is sometimes funny (in a good way) and decant for this type of game ( from A to B storyline with ofc happy ending). Now, to the bad things, game is really short, I got 5 hours out of it, you might get more if you want to complete it 100%. No Man's sky is a game I actually like, but it still has some issues you should be warned about: I think it's still really shaky at 60$, some people may be ok paying that much, but I reccomend waiting for a sale. The PC port improved but it's still pretty bad, and it has a few annoying bugs. The biggest complaint you may have though, is how the game sounds compared to what it is. No Man's Sky is NOT an epic and insanely complex space sim like some of the marketing would have you believe, it's more of a walking sim in the same vein as Journey with some really large sandbox/space sim touches. That said, the updates have heavily improved the game. It now has a surprisingly good story with telltale style choices (I know that sounds ridiculous but it's true), a new quest system which adds a lot of much needed purpose, base building, freighters, and a basic but nice multiplayer functionality. In short, buy the game if it's on sale and you like Journey and/or Elite: Dangerous.
The main reason I'm reccomending the game though, (outside of it being pretty good now) is because companies should be rewarded for fixing their screwups, so few of them do, so I feel people should heavily encourage this kind of thing when it happens, just so it looks like there's insentive for other devs to fix things in the future.

Remember Me gets a bad rap. It's a really fun action adventure that is largely underrated because people want it to be something it's not. First of all it's a linear story. Yes it takes place in a futuristic Paris, no you can't explore where ever you want. As much as we all want it to be an open world game it's not. Now if you can get past that what you'll find is that Remember Me has a rich and detailed story and some elements that make it a really fun game.
As Nilin, a memory hunter, you're up against the company Memorize. Think 30th century Umbrella Corp. There's a revolution going on and you're public enemy number 1. In addition to leading a one man rebellion you're also piecing together Nilin's fractured past. Plenty of story to keep you entertained.
The graphics are incredibly detailed as you explore a diverse world, from the underground sewers to posh futuristic apartment complexes and sterile offices. A lot of work went into realizing the impressive environments. And even in non-movie sequences the visuals are stunning.
As for gameplay there's a mixed bag of tricks. The main thing about this that sets it apart from the rest of the pretty 3rd person adventure games is the ability to remix people's memories of events. However, those events are few and far between as there's only 4 instances of doing that in the entire game. And because it's a fairly short game, only took me about 15 hours to finish it feels like something with a lot of potential that could have gotten a lot more prominent use in a larger game.
This game also boasted the idea of being able to create your own fighting combos. This is also a place where I think a bit of false advertising or lost in translation fell flat. There's only 4 fighting combinations. You can edit what you do when you press a button but not much else. I feel like Sleeping Dogs had more variety in fighting where this game just pretends to give you a very limited variety. Also if you're reading this DO NOT BUY THE DLC. It just unlocks a handful of extra move types. You still have the same 4 combos just you're given a few extra designations. IMO it's not worth $4 but I thankfully bought it at 75% off so the sting of realizing it's cheap and worthless doesn't hurt that much.
That being said it's a cool game. If you see it on sale and want to play something that's a little bit different then go for it. You'll have some fun though quickly fleeting, it's got a nice story, good soundtrack and voice acting. It's not terribly challenging but you're playing it for the story mostly and that at least lives up to some of the hype.
Unforgettable for what it does badly, forgettable for what it does well.
